title: Audit Report
health_method: This score measures source code security only. Formula: 100 ÷ (1 + P ÷ (20 × F)), where P = sum of penalties and F = LOC factor (lines of code ÷ 1,000, minimum 1). Each Security finding costs: CRITICAL (10), HIGH (5), MEDIUM (2), LOW (1). LOC weighting normalizes the score by project size. Non-security categories (Architecture, UI, UX, Maintenance) are not factored in.
top_files_subtitle: Ranked by severity score (CRITICAL×10, HIGH×5, MEDIUM×2, LOW×1)
severity_distribution_subtitle: Number of issues per severity level (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO)
by_category_subtitle: Number of issues per audit category (Security, Architecture, UI, UX, Maintenance) — not to be confused with severity above
category_examples_subtitle: The most frequent issue in each category, with a real instance detected in this project and the generic fix for this type of pattern.
category_example_fix: How to fix this type of pattern
category_example_bridge: 💡 This rule flags a broader principle than just this snippet: {solution}. The example below illustrates the general fix principle, not necessarily your exact case.

chart_subtitles.database_history: Tables, columns and changes over 10 audits

validations_intro: This section lists positive findings from the audit. Each item represents a verified security or architecture good practice in your code.
success_cat_no_critical: {cat}: no CRITICAL or HIGH finding — category within acceptable thresholds.
success_fixtures_coverage: Fixture coverage: {rate}% — all rules validated by test cases.
no_issues_category: No issues detected in this category.

fixtures_explanation: Each detection rule is tested against two types of test files (fixtures): vulnerable fixtures contain a known security pattern and must trigger a detection, while clean fixtures contain safe code and must not trigger any alert. This section measures the reliability of every rule.
fixtures_true_positives_desc: Vulnerable fixtures correctly detected by the rule
fixtures_true_negatives_desc: Clean fixtures correctly ignored (no false alert)
fixtures_false_negatives_desc: Vulnerable fixtures missed by the rule (detection failure)
deps_warn_no_distribution: Dependency incompatible with the audit .venv Python version. CVE scan was interrupted.
deps_warn_no_distribution_fix: Update the dependency to a compatible version, or run pip-audit with a Python version compatible with the project.
deps_warn_timeout_fix: Check your network connection or reduce the number of dependencies.
deps_warn_tool_missing_fix: Install the indicated tool to enable CVE scanning.
deps_warn_generic_fix: Check the dependency file and rerun the audit.

sql_injection_fstring.name: SQL Injection (f-string)
sql_injection_fstring.risk: An attacker can inject malicious SQL and access/modify/delete data.
sql_injection_fstring.solution: Use bound parameters: db.execute(text('SELECT * FROM x WHERE id = :id'), {'id': value})

sql_injection_concat.name: SQL Injection (concat)
sql_injection_concat.risk: String concatenation in SQL queries allows injection.

hardcoded_secret.name: Hardcoded secret
hardcoded_secret.risk: Plain text secrets in code can be exposed via Git repository.
hardcoded_secret.solution: Use environment variables or system_configs in database.

dangerous_eval.name: Dangerous Eval/Exec
dangerous_eval.risk: eval() or exec() with user data allows arbitrary code execution.
dangerous_eval.solution: Never use eval/exec with external data.

debug_mode.name: Debug mode enabled
debug_mode.risk: Debug mode exposes sensitive information (stack traces, variables, paths).
debug_mode.solution: Use debug=False in production, or condition with environment variable.

secret_logged_fstring.name: Secret logged (f-string)
secret_logged_fstring.risk: A secret value is logged via f-string, exposed in logs.
secret_logged_fstring.solution: Never log secrets. Log user ID or hash instead.

secret_logged_arg.name: Secret logged (argument)
secret_logged_arg.risk: A secret variable is passed as argument to the logger.
secret_logged_arg.solution: Never log secrets. Log user ID or hash instead.

http_no_tls.name: HTTP without TLS
http_no_tls.risk: Unencrypted HTTP traffic can be intercepted (man-in-the-middle).
http_no_tls.solution: Use HTTPS for all external URLs.

xss_innerhtml.name: XSS via innerHTML
xss_innerhtml.risk: Direct innerHTML manipulation can inject malicious scripts.
xss_innerhtml.solution: Use textContent or a safe templating system instead of innerHTML.

n_plus_1_query.name: Potential N+1 Query
n_plus_1_query.risk: Database query in loop causes performance issues.
n_plus_1_query.solution: Use eager loading (joinedload) or batch queries.

file_too_long.name: File too long
file_too_long.risk: Very long files are difficult to maintain and understand.

inline_style_js.name: Inline style in JS
inline_style_js.risk: Inline styles bypass CSS system and create inconsistency.
inline_style_js.solution: Use CSS classes from a shared style system.

manual_createelement.name: Manual createElement
manual_createelement.risk: Manual DOM creation is verbose and error-prone.
manual_createelement.solution: Use a templating system or framework for HTML generation.

event_listeners_not_cleaned.name: Event listeners not cleaned
event_listeners_not_cleaned.risk: Event listeners without cleanup cause memory leaks.
event_listeners_not_cleaned.solution: Store references and call removeEventListener on destroy.

dom_manipulation_loop.name: DOM manipulation in loop
dom_manipulation_loop.risk: Multiple DOM updates in loop cause reflows and poor performance.
dom_manipulation_loop.solution: Build HTML string first, then single innerHTML assignment.

svg_inline_html.name: Inline SVG in HTML
svg_inline_html.risk: Inline SVGs bloat HTML and are hard to maintain.
svg_inline_html.solution: Use an icon system or external SVG sprites.

hardcoded_ui_string.name: Hardcoded UI string
hardcoded_ui_string.risk: User-facing text hardcoded in source code breaks internationalization and complicates translation workflows.
hardcoded_ui_string.solution: Extract strings to i18n resource files and use translation functions (t(), i18n(), gettext()).
hardcoded_ui_string.benefit: Full multilingual support, centralized text management, easier translation updates.

console_log_residual.name: Residual console.log
console_log_residual.risk: Console logs in production expose debug information.
console_log_residual.solution: Remove console.log or use a logging system.

button_no_aria.name: Button without aria-label
button_no_aria.risk: Icon-only buttons are inaccessible to screen readers.

input_no_label.name: Input without label
input_no_label.solution: Add associated label element or aria-label.

todo_unresolved.name: Unresolved TODO/FIXME
todo_unresolved.solution: Resolve or create a ticket for tracking.

py_commented_out_code.name: Commented-out code (dead code)
py_commented_out_code.risk: Commented-out code is dead code that pollutes the codebase, misleads readers about intent, and is never tested or updated. It accumulates technical debt over time.
py_commented_out_code.solution: Delete the commented-out code. If it might be needed later, use version control to retrieve it.
py_commented_out_code.benefit: Cleaner, more readable codebase — every line of code is either active or absent, no ambiguity.

py_magic_value_comparison.name: Magic number comparison
py_magic_value_comparison.risk: Comparing directly to unexplained numeric literals (magic numbers) makes the code hard to understand and maintain. The meaning of the number is not clear from context.
py_magic_value_comparison.solution: Extract the numeric literal into a named constant that describes its meaning, e.g. MAX_RETRY_COUNT = 300.
py_magic_value_comparison.benefit: Self-documenting code — the intent behind each numeric value is explicit and searchable.

py_too_many_arguments.name: Too many function arguments (6+)
py_too_many_arguments.risk: A function with 6 or more parameters is hard to call correctly, hard to test, and often indicates a violation of the Single Responsibility Principle.
py_too_many_arguments.solution: Group related parameters into a dataclass, TypedDict, or a dedicated configuration object. Alternatively, split the function into smaller, focused functions.
py_too_many_arguments.benefit: Simpler function signatures, easier testing, better alignment with the Single Responsibility Principle.

py_global_statement.name: Global statement inside function
py_global_statement.risk: Using the global statement inside a function creates hidden dependencies on module-level state. It makes functions harder to test, understand, and reuse.
py_global_statement.solution: Pass the value as a parameter and return the modified value. For shared state, use a class instance or a dedicated state container.
py_global_statement.benefit: Pure functions are predictable, testable, and composable — each call returns the same result for the same input.

py_too_many_nested_blocks.name: Excessive nesting depth (6+ levels)
py_too_many_nested_blocks.risk: Code nested more than 5 levels deep is extremely difficult to read, test, and maintain. Deep nesting is a symptom of code that tries to do too much in a single block.
py_too_many_nested_blocks.solution: Apply early return / guard clauses to reduce nesting. Extract deeply nested logic into dedicated helper functions.
py_too_many_nested_blocks.benefit: Code that reads linearly from top to bottom is easier to understand, test, and modify than deeply nested pyramids.

py_bare_except.name: Bare except clause (no exception type)
py_bare_except.risk: A bare except clause catches all exceptions including SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt, and GeneratorExit, which should never be caught silently. It hides bugs and makes debugging nearly impossible.
py_bare_except.solution: Always catch a specific exception type (e.g. except ValueError, except (IOError, OSError)). Use except Exception as e if you need a broad catch but still want to log or inspect the error.
py_bare_except.benefit: Precise exception handling — only expected errors are caught, unexpected failures propagate correctly and are visible in logs.

test_failed.name: Failed unit test
test_failed.solution: Fix the test or the underlying code.

test_error.name: Unit test error
test_error.solution: Fix the test setup or dependencies.

unsafe_deserialization.name: Unsafe deserialization
unsafe_deserialization.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary code via malicious serialized data (pickle, yaml.load).
unsafe_deserialization.solution: Use json.loads() or yaml.safe_load(). Never deserialize untrusted data with pickle.

weak_crypto.name: Weak cryptographic algorithm
weak_crypto.risk: MD5 and SHA1 are vulnerable to collisions and must not be used for secure hashing.
weak_crypto.solution: Use SHA-256/SHA-512 for hashing, bcrypt/argon2 for passwords.
weak_crypto.benefit: Resistance to collision and brute-force attacks (CWE-328).

insecure_random.name: Insecure RNG
insecure_random.risk: Math.random() is predictable and must not be used for tokens, OTPs or keys.
insecure_random.solution: Use crypto.getRandomValues() or crypto.randomUUID() for sensitive values.
insecure_random.benefit: Unpredictable tokens and keys, resistant to attacks (CWE-330).

unvalidated_input.name: Unvalidated input (OS injection)
unvalidated_input.risk: Using shell=True with subprocess allows OS command injection.
unvalidated_input.solution: Use subprocess with shell=False and pass arguments as a list.

verbose_exception.name: Verbose exception
verbose_exception.risk: Exposed stack traces reveal internal application structure to attackers.
verbose_exception.solution: Log the exception server-side and return a generic message to the user.

catch_all_exception.name: Catch-all exception
catch_all_exception.risk: A bare except catches SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, masking critical errors.
catch_all_exception.solution: Use except Exception or specific types (ValueError, IOError, etc.).
catch_all_exception.benefit: Better error handling and easier debugging (CWE-396).

client_side_auth.name: Client-side access control
client_side_auth.risk: Authorization checks in localStorage are bypassable via DevTools.
client_side_auth.solution: Always verify permissions server-side. The client only adapts the display.

homebrew_auth.name: Homebrew authentication
homebrew_auth.risk: Direct password comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks and bypasses best practices (hashing, salting).
homebrew_auth.solution: Use bcrypt.checkpw() or passlib.verify() to compare passwords.
homebrew_auth.benefit: Authentication resistant to timing and brute-force attacks (CWE-287).

predictable_session.name: Predictable token/session
predictable_session.risk: The random module is predictable (PRNG). Generated tokens can be guessed by an attacker.
predictable_session.solution: Use secrets.token_hex() or secrets.token_urlsafe() for tokens and sessions.

dynamic_import.name: Dynamic import
dynamic_import.risk: __import__() or importlib.import_module() with user variable allows loading arbitrary code.
dynamic_import.solution: Use a whitelist of allowed modules or avoid dynamic imports.

deprecated_api.name: Deprecated API
deprecated_api.risk: os.popen(), tempfile.mktemp() and os.system() are deprecated and present security risks.
deprecated_api.solution: Use subprocess.run() instead of os.popen()/os.system(), tempfile.mkstemp() instead of mktemp().

race_condition.name: Race condition (TOCTOU)
race_condition.risk: Checking file existence then opening creates an exploitable time window (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use).
race_condition.solution: Use try/except with open() directly, or os.open() with O_CREAT|O_EXCL flags.
race_condition.benefit: Elimination of file race condition vulnerabilities (CWE-367).

vulnerable_dependency.name: Vulnerable Dependency
vulnerable_dependency.risk: Known CVE in dependency — may allow remote code execution, data leak, or denial of service.
vulnerable_dependency.solution: Update to the fixed version listed in the advisory.

unpinned_dependency.name: Unpinned Dependency
unpinned_dependency.risk: Dependency without version pin may install vulnerable versions silently.
unpinned_dependency.solution: Pin exact versions in requirements.txt (package==x.y.z) or package-lock.json.
unpinned_dependency.benefit: Reproducible builds and protection against supply chain attacks (CWE-1357).

non_compliant_license.name: Non-compliant License
non_compliant_license.risk: Dependency uses a license not in the approved list, which may cause legal compliance issues.
non_compliant_license.solution: Replace the dependency with one using an approved SPDX license, or add the license to the allowed list.
non_compliant_license.benefit: Legal compliance, reduced risk of license violations in production.

img_no_alt.name: Image without alt text
img_no_alt.risk: Images without alternative text are inaccessible to screen readers and visually impaired users.
img_no_alt.solution: Add a descriptive alt attribute on every tag.

positive_tabindex.name: Positive tabindex
positive_tabindex.risk: A tabindex > 0 disrupts the natural keyboard navigation order, making the page unpredictable.
positive_tabindex.solution: Use tabindex="0" to add an element to the flow, or tabindex="-1" for programmatic focus.
positive_tabindex.benefit: WCAG 2.4.3 compliance — logical and predictable focus order.

focus_outline_removed.name: Focus outline removed
focus_outline_removed.risk: Removing the outline prevents keyboard users from seeing which element has focus.
focus_outline_removed.solution: Do not remove outline. If the default style is unsuitable, replace it with a visible alternative.
focus_outline_removed.benefit: WCAG 2.4.7 compliance — focus always visible for keyboard navigation.

jsx_img_missing_alt.name: JSX image without alt prop (WCAG 1.1.1)
jsx_img_missing_alt.risk: A JSX without an alt prop is inaccessible to screen readers and visually impaired users.
jsx_img_missing_alt.solution: Add an alt prop with descriptive text for informative images, or alt="" for purely decorative images.
jsx_img_missing_alt.benefit: WCAG 1.1.1 compliance — all images have a textual alternative accessible to assistive technologies.

jsx_anchor_href_invalid.name: JSX link with invalid href (href="#" or javascript:)
jsx_anchor_href_invalid.risk: Using href="#" or href="javascript:void(0)" as a click handler breaks keyboard navigation and screen readers. A <button> should be used for actions.
jsx_anchor_href_invalid.solution: Use a <button> element for actions (not navigation). Reserve <a> for actual navigation links with a valid URL.
jsx_anchor_href_invalid.benefit: WCAG 2.4.4 and 4.1.2 compliance — interactive elements have the correct semantics for their purpose.

jsx_label_missing_control.name: JSX label without associated control (missing htmlFor)
jsx_label_missing_control.risk: A JSX <label> without a htmlFor prop is not programmatically linked to its form control. Screen readers cannot associate the label with the input.
jsx_label_missing_control.solution: Add a htmlFor prop matching the id of the associated input, or nest the input directly inside the label.
jsx_label_missing_control.benefit: WCAG 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 compliance — the label is announced by screen readers when the input is focused.

jsx_tabindex_positive.name: Positive tabIndex (JSX, WCAG 2.4.3)
jsx_tabindex_positive.risk: A positive tabIndex value overrides the natural document tab order, making keyboard navigation unpredictable.
jsx_tabindex_positive.solution: Use tabIndex={0} to add an element to the natural tab order, or tabIndex={-1} for programmatic focus only. Never use values > 0.
jsx_tabindex_positive.benefit: WCAG 2.4.3 compliance — focus order follows a logical and predictable sequence matching the visual layout.

jsx_no_autofocus.name: autoFocus used (JSX)
jsx_no_autofocus.risk: The autoFocus prop automatically moves keyboard focus when a component mounts, disrupting the natural focus flow for screen reader and keyboard users.
jsx_no_autofocus.solution: Remove autoFocus. Manage focus programmatically with React refs and useEffect at the right moment.
jsx_no_autofocus.benefit: Predictable focus behavior — users always know where they are on the page.

jsx_no_access_key.name: accessKey used (JSX)
jsx_no_access_key.risk: The accessKey prop creates keyboard shortcuts that conflict with browser and screen reader shortcuts, causing confusion and unexpected behavior.
jsx_no_access_key.solution: Remove the accessKey attribute. Implement a custom keyboard shortcut system via event listeners if needed.
jsx_no_access_key.benefit: Consistent keyboard navigation — no unexpected focus jumps or conflicts with browser shortcuts.

autoplay_media.name: Autoplaying media
autoplay_media.risk: Auto-playing videos or audio disrupt users, especially those using screen readers.
autoplay_media.solution: Remove the autoplay attribute and let the user start playback manually.

pull_request_target_checkout.name: pull_request_target with fork checkout
pull_request_target_checkout.risk: Checking out PR head in a pull_request_target workflow grants write access and secrets to untrusted code.
pull_request_target_checkout.solution: Never checkout the PR head ref in pull_request_target. Use workflow_run or separate workflows for trusted operations.
pull_request_target_checkout.benefit: Protection against supply chain attacks via malicious PRs (OWASP CI-CD-01).

gha_expression_injection.name: GitHub Actions expression injection
gha_expression_injection.risk: Using ${{ }} with user-controlled data (issue title, PR body, comment) in run: blocks enables arbitrary command execution.
gha_expression_injection.solution: Assign the expression to an environment variable first, then reference it as $ENV_VAR in the script.
gha_expression_injection.benefit: Prevention of command injection in CI/CD pipelines (OWASP CI-CD-01).

gha_excessive_permissions.name: Excessive workflow permissions
gha_excessive_permissions.risk: permissions: write-all grants maximum privileges to the GITHUB_TOKEN, violating least-privilege principle.
gha_excessive_permissions.solution: Declare granular permissions per scope (contents: read, issues: write, etc.).
gha_excessive_permissions.benefit: Least-privilege enforcement, limiting blast radius of compromised workflows (OWASP CI-CD-05).

gha_missing_permissions.name: Missing permissions block
gha_missing_permissions.risk: Without explicit permissions:, the GITHUB_TOKEN inherits the repository's default (often write-all).
gha_missing_permissions.solution: Add a top-level permissions: block with minimal scopes needed.
gha_missing_permissions.benefit: Explicit security posture, protection against accidental privilege escalation (OWASP CI-CD-05).

gha_unguarded_comment_trigger.name: Unguarded comment trigger
gha_unguarded_comment_trigger.risk: issue_comment workflows without author_association check allow any user to trigger potentially privileged actions.
gha_unguarded_comment_trigger.solution: Add a condition checking github.event.comment.author_association (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR).
gha_unguarded_comment_trigger.benefit: Prevention of unauthorized workflow execution by external contributors.

unpinned_action_version.name: Unpinned action version
unpinned_action_version.risk: Referencing actions by mutable tag (v1, main) exposes the pipeline to tag-hijacking supply chain attacks.
unpinned_action_version.solution: Pin actions to a full commit SHA (40 hex chars). Add a comment with the version for readability.
unpinned_action_version.benefit: Immunity against tag-hijacking attacks like the Codecov/tj-actions incidents (OWASP CI-CD-09).

gitlab_unsafe_variables.name: Unprotected GitLab CI variable
gitlab_unsafe_variables.risk: Sensitive variables (passwords, tokens) defined in plain text in .gitlab-ci.yml are exposed in logs and forks.
gitlab_unsafe_variables.solution: Use GitLab CI/CD masked and protected variables (Settings > CI/CD > Variables).
gitlab_unsafe_variables.benefit: Secret protection in CI/CD logs and fork environments.

workflow_not_in_codeowners.name: Deployment workflows anyone can change without review
workflow_not_in_codeowners.risk: Your GitHub Actions workflows (the files in .github/workflows/ that build and deploy your code) can be changed by any contributor without anyone reviewing the change. Someone could alter how your code is deployed, or read its secrets, unnoticed.
workflow_not_in_codeowners.solution: Create the file .github/CODEOWNERS (GitHub reads in it who must approve changes to which files) with the line /.github/workflows/ @your-team, then turn on "Require review from Code Owners" in the repository's branch protection settings.
workflow_not_in_codeowners.benefit: Every change to how your code is built and deployed must be approved by a person you chose.

gha_secret_in_log.name: Secret printed in workflow log
gha_secret_in_log.risk: Printing a GitHub Actions secret directly in a run: block exposes its value in workflow logs.
gha_secret_in_log.solution: Never echo secrets directly. Use them only as environment variables passed to the command.
gha_secret_in_log.benefit: Prevents secret leakage in CI/CD logs accessible to all repository contributors.

gha_deprecated_commands.name: Deprecated workflow commands
gha_deprecated_commands.risk: Deprecated workflow commands ::set-env:: and ::add-path:: allow environment injection attacks via log output parsing (CVE-2020-15228).
gha_deprecated_commands.solution: Replace ::set-env:: with 'echo NAME=VALUE >> $GITHUB_ENV' and ::add-path:: with 'echo PATH >> $GITHUB_PATH'.
gha_deprecated_commands.benefit: Eliminates environment injection risk from the deprecated workflow command API.

gha_artifact_poisoning.name: Artifact poisoning via workflow_run
gha_artifact_poisoning.risk: Downloading artifacts in a workflow_run context without integrity verification allows artifact poisoning if the source workflow is compromised.
gha_artifact_poisoning.solution: Verify artifact integrity with checksums after download, or restrict the triggering workflow to trusted refs only.
gha_artifact_poisoning.benefit: Prevents supply chain attacks via malicious artifacts injected into the CI/CD pipeline.

gha_self_hosted_runner.name: Self-hosted runner on public repository
gha_self_hosted_runner.risk: Self-hosted runners on public repositories allow any fork contributor to execute arbitrary code on your infrastructure via a pull request.
gha_self_hosted_runner.solution: For public repositories, use GitHub-hosted runners. If self-hosted is required, restrict to private repositories with branch policies.
gha_self_hosted_runner.benefit: Eliminates the risk of infrastructure compromise through malicious PRs on public repositories (OWASP CI-CD-06).

ci_curl_pipe_bash.name: Remote script piped to shell
ci_curl_pipe_bash.risk: Piping a remote script directly into a shell executes arbitrary code without inspection, enabling supply chain attacks if the remote resource is compromised.
ci_curl_pipe_bash.solution: Download the script to a file first, inspect it, then execute it explicitly after verification.
ci_curl_pipe_bash.benefit: Prevents arbitrary code execution from compromised remote resources in the CI/CD pipeline (OWASP CI-CD-09).

ci_insecure_download.name: Insecure HTTP download in CI/CD
ci_insecure_download.risk: Downloading resources over plain HTTP in CI/CD pipelines exposes the build to man-in-the-middle attacks and dependency tampering.
ci_insecure_download.solution: Always use HTTPS (https://) for downloads in CI/CD pipelines. Verify checksums after download.
ci_insecure_download.benefit: Ensures build dependencies are downloaded over an encrypted channel, preventing tampering during transit.

hardcoded_secret_cicd.name: Hardcoded secret in CI/CD configuration
hardcoded_secret_cicd.risk: A secret value (password, token, API key) is hardcoded directly in the CI/CD configuration file and exposed to all repository contributors.
hardcoded_secret_cicd.solution: Move secrets to your CI/CD platform's secret store (GitHub Secrets, GitLab CI Variables) and reference them via environment variables.
hardcoded_secret_cicd.benefit: Eliminates credential exposure in version control history and CI/CD logs (OWASP CI-CD-04, CWE-798).

docker_latest_tag.name: Docker image with :latest tag
docker_latest_tag.risk: Using the :latest Docker image tag in CI/CD pipelines causes unpredictable builds as the referenced image may change without notice.
docker_latest_tag.solution: Pin Docker images to a specific version tag or digest (e.g., node:20.11-alpine or node@sha256:...).
docker_latest_tag.benefit: Ensures reproducible and secure builds by preventing silent image upgrades in the CI/CD pipeline.

gitlab_allow_failure_security.name: Security job with allow_failure: true
gitlab_allow_failure_security.risk: Setting allow_failure: true on a security scanning job allows the pipeline to succeed even when vulnerabilities are found, silencing critical alerts.
gitlab_allow_failure_security.solution: Remove allow_failure: true from security jobs, or configure exit codes to distinguish errors from vulnerability findings.
gitlab_allow_failure_security.benefit: Ensures security vulnerabilities block the pipeline and cannot be silently ignored in production deployments.

gitlab_script_secrets_echo.name: GitLab CI token printed to log
gitlab_script_secrets_echo.risk: Printing GitLab CI built-in authentication tokens to the job log exposes them to anyone with log access, enabling repository or registry access.
gitlab_script_secrets_echo.solution: Remove echo statements that print authentication tokens. Use them directly in commands without echoing.
gitlab_script_secrets_echo.benefit: Prevents credential leakage in CI/CD job logs exploitable for unauthorized repository or container registry access.

gha_credentials_on_disk.name: Git credentials persisted on disk
gha_credentials_on_disk.risk: Setting persist-credentials: true in actions/checkout stores the GitHub token in .git/config, exposing it to any subsequent step or action reading the filesystem.
gha_credentials_on_disk.solution: Set persist-credentials: false explicitly and pass credentials only to steps that require them.
gha_credentials_on_disk.benefit: Prevents credential leakage to post-checkout steps, reducing the blast radius of a compromised action.

gha_github_env_write.name: Untrusted data written to GITHUB_ENV
gha_github_env_write.risk: Writing untrusted event data (PR title, issue body, comment) directly to $GITHUB_ENV allows environment variable injection into all subsequent steps.
gha_github_env_write.solution: Sanitize event data before writing to $GITHUB_ENV, or pass it via env: block on the specific step that needs it.
gha_github_env_write.benefit: Prevents environment variable injection attacks affecting all subsequent steps in the workflow.

ci_docker_privileged.name: Privileged Docker container in CI/CD
ci_docker_privileged.risk: Running a CI/CD container with privileged mode grants full access to the host kernel, devices, and namespaces — equivalent to root on the host system.
ci_docker_privileged.solution: Remove the --privileged flag. Use specific Linux capabilities (--cap-add) only for exact functionality required.
ci_docker_privileged.benefit: Prevents container escape attacks and limits blast radius of a compromised CI/CD job to the container.

gha_dangerous_artefact.name: Sensitive files uploaded as artifact
gha_dangerous_artefact.risk: Uploading artifacts containing private keys, certificates, .env files or credentials exposes them to anyone with read access to the repository's artifact storage.
gha_dangerous_artefact.solution: Exclude sensitive files from artifact upload paths. Use explicit include patterns instead of wildcards.
gha_dangerous_artefact.benefit: Prevents unintentional exposure of cryptographic material and credentials through CI/CD artifact storage.

gha_insecure_commands_env.name: Insecure workflow commands enabled
gha_insecure_commands_env.risk: Setting ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS to true re-enables deprecated workflow commands that allow environment injection attacks (CVE-2020-15228).
gha_insecure_commands_env.solution: Remove ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS. Use $GITHUB_ENV and $GITHUB_PATH file-based APIs instead.
gha_insecure_commands_env.benefit: Eliminates the attack surface introduced by insecure workflow commands.

gha_cache_poisoning.name: Cache poisoning risk in release workflow
gha_cache_poisoning.risk: Using build caches during a release workflow allows cache poisoning — a compromised cache entry can inject malicious code into a published artifact.
gha_cache_poisoning.solution: Disable caching in release workflows (cache: false) or use isolated environments without shared cache.
gha_cache_poisoning.benefit: Ensures published artifacts are built from source only, preventing supply chain attacks (OWASP CI-CD-09).

dependabot_insecure_exec.name: Dependabot insecure external code execution
dependabot_insecure_exec.risk: insecure-external-code-execution: allow permits running unverified external scripts during dependency updates, enabling supply chain attacks.
dependabot_insecure_exec.benefit: Prevents execution of unverified external code during automated dependency updates.

gha_github_app_no_revoke.name: GitHub App token not revoked after job
gha_github_app_no_revoke.risk: skip-token-revoke: true prevents automatic token revocation, leaving the GitHub App token valid and exploitable until it naturally expires.
gha_github_app_no_revoke.solution: Remove skip-token-revoke: true to ensure tokens are automatically revoked when the job completes.
gha_github_app_no_revoke.benefit: Ensures GitHub App tokens are automatically invalidated as soon as the workflow job finishes.

gha_confused_deputy.name: Confused deputy auto-merge bypass
gha_confused_deputy.risk: Using github.actor to gate auto-merge decisions is vulnerable — an attacker can create an account whose name matches the actor check, bypassing the intended restriction.
gha_confused_deputy.solution: Use github.event.pull_request.user.login instead. Prefer repository environments with required reviewers for deployment gates.
gha_confused_deputy.benefit: Prevents auto-merge bypass attacks where an attacker impersonates a trusted bot.

gha_job_all_secrets.name: All secrets serialized in workflow
gha_job_all_secrets.risk: toJSON(secrets) serializes all secrets — including organization secrets — into a single string that can be logged or exfiltrated by a compromised step.
gha_job_all_secrets.solution: Reference only the specific secrets needed (${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}). Never serialize the entire secrets context.
gha_job_all_secrets.benefit: Limits blast radius to only explicitly referenced secrets, following least privilege principle.

ci_netcat_reverse_shell.name: Netcat reverse shell in CI/CD script
ci_netcat_reverse_shell.risk: Use of netcat (nc) with an IP address in a CI/CD script is a strong indicator of a reverse shell or data exfiltration attempt.
ci_netcat_reverse_shell.solution: Remove the netcat command. Use purpose-built tools with explicit allow-listing for legitimate network testing.
ci_netcat_reverse_shell.benefit: Detects potential reverse shells and data exfiltration channels in CI/CD pipeline scripts.

gha_secrets_bypass_redaction.name: Secrets redaction bypass via JSON
gha_secrets_bypass_redaction.risk: toJSON(secrets) or fromJSON(secrets.*) bypasses GitHub's automatic log redaction, causing secret values to appear in plain text in job logs.
gha_secrets_bypass_redaction.solution: Avoid fromJSON/toJSON with the secrets context. Access individual secrets directly via ${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}.
gha_secrets_bypass_redaction.benefit: Ensures secret values remain redacted in CI/CD job logs even in complex expressions.

gha_actor_check_bypass.name: Bypassable actor-based security gate
gha_actor_check_bypass.risk: Using github.actor as a security gate is bypassable — any user can create an account whose name matches the check.
gha_actor_check_bypass.solution: Prefer github.event.sender.login for PR/issue events, or use environment protection rules with required reviewers.
gha_actor_check_bypass.benefit: Prevents security bypass through account name spoofing in actor-based workflow conditions.

ci_debug_trace_enabled.name: CI/CD debug logging enabled
ci_debug_trace_enabled.risk: Debug logging in CI/CD pipelines exposes sensitive data including environment variables, secret values, internal URLs, and tokens in job logs.
ci_debug_trace_enabled.solution: Remove debug variables from production workflow configurations. Use debug mode only temporarily in development branches.
ci_debug_trace_enabled.benefit: Prevents accidental exposure of sensitive runtime data through verbose CI/CD logs.

gha_secrets_without_environment.name: Secrets used without environment gate on risky trigger
gha_secrets_without_environment.risk: Using non-GITHUB_TOKEN secrets in workflows triggered by risky events (pull_request_target, issue_comment, workflow_run) without an environment gate allows untrusted code to access sensitive secrets.
gha_secrets_without_environment.solution: Add environment: protection to jobs using secrets on risky event triggers. Configure required reviewers on the environment.
gha_secrets_without_environment.benefit: Ensures sensitive secrets are only accessible after explicit human approval when triggered by external actors.

gha_unsound_condition.name: Unsound if: condition with block scalar
gha_unsound_condition.risk: Using a YAML block scalar (| or >) for an if: condition includes a trailing newline, making the condition always evaluate to true regardless of the intended logic.
gha_unsound_condition.solution: Write if: conditions as single-line expressions. Never use | or > block scalars for conditional expressions.
gha_unsound_condition.benefit: Prevents security bypass caused by YAML block scalar semantics making if: conditions always true.

gha_workflow_dispatch_inputs.name: workflow_dispatch with user inputs
gha_workflow_dispatch_inputs.risk: workflow_dispatch with user-defined inputs can affect build output, breaking reproducibility — the same commit may produce different artifacts depending on dispatch inputs.
gha_workflow_dispatch_inputs.solution: For release workflows, prefer triggers without user inputs (push to tags, release event). If inputs are needed, validate and sanitize them.
gha_workflow_dispatch_inputs.benefit: Ensures build reproducibility and prevents users from injecting unexpected parameters.

gha_version_comment_missing.name: Pinned action SHA without version comment
gha_version_comment_missing.risk: Pinning an action to a SHA without a version comment makes it impossible to know which version is pinned without looking up the hash.
gha_version_comment_missing.solution: Add a comment with the version tag next to the SHA (e.g., uses: actions/checkout@b4ffde65 # v4.1.1).
gha_version_comment_missing.benefit: Makes pinned action versions human-readable for security audits without losing the supply chain protection of SHA pinning.

gha_local_action.name: Local action usage
gha_local_action.risk: Local actions (uses: ./) execute code from the current repository checkout — any contributor with write access who modifies the action can affect all workflows that use it.
gha_local_action.solution: Ensure local actions are covered by CODEOWNERS review requirements. Document the action's purpose with a README.
gha_local_action.benefit: Makes local action usage explicit for security reviewers to audit all locally executed workflow code.

gitlab_double_pipeline.name: GitLab CI duplicate pipeline rules
gitlab_double_pipeline.risk: Duplicate pipeline source rules for merge_request_event create double pipelines — both MR and branch pipelines run for the same commit, doubling CI resource usage.
gitlab_double_pipeline.solution: Use workflow rules with $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event" exclusively, or add a when: never rule for branch pipelines.
gitlab_double_pipeline.benefit: Prevents wasteful double pipeline execution and potential race conditions between MR and branch pipelines.

sql_injection_concat_java.name: SQL injection (Java concatenation)
sql_injection_concat_java.risk: String concatenation in JDBC executeQuery/executeUpdate allows SQL injection.
sql_injection_concat_java.benefit: Immunity against SQL injection attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_format_java.name: SQL injection (Java String.format)
sql_injection_format_java.risk: String.format with SQL keywords builds dynamic queries vulnerable to injection.
sql_injection_format_java.solution: Use PreparedStatement with parameterized queries instead of String.format.
sql_injection_format_java.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection via formatted strings (OWASP A03).

unsafe_deserialization_java.name: Unsafe deserialization (Java)
unsafe_deserialization_java.risk: ObjectInputStream.readObject() without validation allows arbitrary code running.
unsafe_deserialization_java.solution: Use ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+) or a whitelist of allowed classes. Prefer JSON/XML serialization.
unsafe_deserialization_java.benefit: Protection against deserialization attacks (OWASP A08, CWE-502).

xxe_injection.name: XXE injection
xxe_injection.risk: DocumentBuilderFactory without setFeature allows XML External Entity attacks (file read, SSRF).
xxe_injection.solution: Disable DTDs and external entities: factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, true).
xxe_injection.benefit: Prevention of XXE attacks (OWASP A05, CWE-611).

command_injection_java.name: Command injection (Java)
command_injection_java.risk: Runtime.getRuntime() with user input allows arbitrary OS command running.
command_injection_java.solution: Use ProcessBuilder with argument list (no shell interpretation). Validate and whitelist inputs.
command_injection_java.benefit: Prevention of OS command injection (OWASP A03, CWE-78).

spring_csrf_disabled.name: Spring CSRF disabled
spring_csrf_disabled.risk: Disabling CSRF protection allows cross-site request forgery attacks on state-changing endpoints.
spring_csrf_disabled.solution: Keep CSRF enabled for browser-facing endpoints. Only disable for stateless APIs with token auth.
spring_csrf_disabled.benefit: Protection against CSRF attacks (OWASP A01, CWE-352).

spring_cors_permissive.name: Permissive CORS configuration
spring_cors_permissive.risk: allowedOrigins("*") or unrestricted @CrossOrigin allows any domain to make authenticated requests.
spring_cors_permissive.solution: Specify allowed origins matching your frontend domains.
spring_cors_permissive.benefit: Prevention of cross-origin data theft (OWASP A01, CWE-942).

weak_crypto_java.name: Weak cryptography (Java)
weak_crypto_java.risk: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken — vulnerable to collision attacks.
weak_crypto_java.solution: Use SHA-256 or SHA-3 (MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")). For passwords, use BCrypt/Argon2.

weak_random_java.name: Weak random (Java)
weak_random_java.risk: java.util.Random is predictable — tokens, sessions, and keys generated with it can be guessed.
weak_random_java.solution: Use java.security.SecureRandom for all security-sensitive random generation.

ssl_bypass_java.name: SSL/TLS bypass (Java)
ssl_bypass_java.risk: TrustAllCerts or HostnameVerifier returning true disables certificate validation (MITM attack).
ssl_bypass_java.solution: Use the default SSLContext with proper certificate validation. Never trust all certificates in production.
ssl_bypass_java.benefit: Secure TLS connections with proper certificate validation (OWASP A02, CWE-295).

open_redirect_java.name: Open redirect (Java)
open_redirect_java.risk: sendRedirect with user-controlled parameter allows phishing via trusted domain.
open_redirect_java.solution: Validate redirect URLs against a whitelist of allowed paths/domains.
open_redirect_java.benefit: Prevention of open redirect attacks (OWASP A01, CWE-601).

spel_injection.name: SpEL injection
spel_injection.risk: StandardEvaluationContext with user input allows arbitrary code running via Spring Expression Language.
spel_injection.solution: Use SimpleEvaluationContext instead of StandardEvaluationContext for user-controlled expressions.
spel_injection.benefit: Prevention of remote code running via SpEL (OWASP A03, CVE-2022-22963).

verbose_exception_java.name: Verbose exception (Java)
verbose_exception_java.risk: printStackTrace() exposes internal stack traces, class names, and paths to attackers.
verbose_exception_java.solution: Use a logging framework (SLF4J/Log4j2) with appropriate log levels. Never expose stack traces to users.
verbose_exception_java.benefit: Prevention of information disclosure (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

secret_logged_java.name: Secret logged (Java)
secret_logged_java.risk: Logging passwords, tokens, or API keys exposes secrets in log files and monitoring systems.
secret_logged_java.solution: Never log sensitive data. Use placeholder values or mask secrets before logging.
secret_logged_java.benefit: Secret protection in logs (OWASP A09, CWE-532).

db_logic_controller_java.name: DB logic in controller (Java)
db_logic_controller_java.risk: EntityManager/JdbcTemplate in @Controller violates separation of concerns, making code untestable.
db_logic_controller_java.solution: Move database logic to @Service or @Repository classes. Controllers should only orchestrate.
db_logic_controller_java.benefit: Clean architecture with testable, maintainable layers.

n_plus_1_query_java.name: N+1 query (Java)
n_plus_1_query_java.risk: Database queries inside loops cause N+1 performance issues and heavy database load.
n_plus_1_query_java.solution: Use batch fetching, JOIN FETCH, or @EntityGraph to load related entities in a single query.
n_plus_1_query_java.benefit: Optimized database access, reduced query count and latency.

system_out_java.name: System.out in production (Java)
system_out_java.risk: System.out/err.println bypasses logging framework — no log levels, no rotation, no monitoring.
system_out_java.solution: Use SLF4J/Log4j2 logger with appropriate log levels (debug, info, warn, error).
system_out_java.benefit: Structured, configurable logging with proper monitoring integration.

catch_all_exception_java.name: Generic catch (Java)
catch_all_exception_java.risk: catch(Exception e) swallows all exceptions including runtime errors, hiding bugs.
catch_all_exception_java.solution: Catch specific exception types. Use multi-catch if needed (catch (IOException | SQLException e)).
catch_all_exception_java.benefit: Precise error handling, no hidden failures (CWE-396).

java_too_many_params.name: Too many Java method parameters (6+)
java_too_many_params.risk: A method or constructor with 6 or more parameters is hard to call correctly, hard to test, and often violates the Single Responsibility Principle.
java_too_many_params.solution: Group related parameters into a dedicated value object, record, or builder pattern.
java_too_many_params.benefit: Simpler method signatures, easier testing, better alignment with the Single Responsibility Principle.

java_deep_nesting.name: Excessive nesting depth (Java, 6+ levels)
java_deep_nesting.risk: Code nested more than 5 levels deep is extremely difficult to read, test, and maintain.
java_deep_nesting.solution: Apply early return / guard clauses. Extract deeply nested logic into dedicated private methods.
java_deep_nesting.benefit: Linear code is easier to understand, test, and modify than deeply nested pyramids.

java_empty_catch_block.name: Empty catch block (Java)
java_empty_catch_block.risk: An empty catch block silently swallows exceptions. Bugs become impossible to diagnose in production.
java_empty_catch_block.solution: At minimum, log the exception. Prefer propagating or rethrowing the exception.
java_empty_catch_block.benefit: Every error is visible and traceable — production debugging becomes possible.

java_string_concat_loop.name: String concatenation in loop (Java)
java_string_concat_loop.risk: Concatenating strings with += inside a loop creates a new String object on every iteration, resulting in O(n²) memory allocation.
java_string_concat_loop.solution: Use StringBuilder to build the string. For joining collections, use String.join() or Stream collectors.
java_string_concat_loop.benefit: StringBuilder operations are O(n) instead of O(n²) — dramatically faster for large datasets.

java_public_field.name: Non-constant public field (Java)
java_public_field.risk: A public non-constant field exposes the internal state of a class, breaking encapsulation. Any code can modify it directly.
java_public_field.solution: Make the field private and provide getter/setter methods. For constants, use public static final.
java_public_field.benefit: Proper encapsulation allows internal implementation changes without breaking client code and enables validation in setters.

java_utility_class_constructor.name: Java utility class without private constructor
java_utility_class_constructor.risk: A utility class (Utils, Helper, Constants) without a private constructor can be instantiated, which makes no semantic sense.
java_utility_class_constructor.solution: Add a private constructor to prevent instantiation. Consider making the class final.
java_utility_class_constructor.benefit: Clear API contract — the class is not meant to be instantiated, only its static methods can be called.

sql_injection_concat_csharp.name: SQL injection (C# concatenation)
sql_injection_concat_csharp.risk: String concatenation in SqlCommand/ExecuteSqlRaw allows SQL injection.
sql_injection_concat_csharp.solution: Use parameterized queries with SqlParameter or LINQ/EF Core.
sql_injection_concat_csharp.benefit: Immunity against SQL injection attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-89, SCS0002).

unsafe_deserialization_csharp.name: Unsafe deserialization (C#)
unsafe_deserialization_csharp.risk: BinaryFormatter and TypeNameHandling.All allow arbitrary code running via crafted payloads.
unsafe_deserialization_csharp.solution: Use System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json with TypeNameHandling.None. Never use BinaryFormatter (CA2300).
unsafe_deserialization_csharp.benefit: Protection against deserialization attacks (OWASP A08, CWE-502, SCS0028).

xxe_injection_csharp.name: XXE injection (C#)
xxe_injection_csharp.risk: DtdProcessing.Parse enables XML External Entity attacks (file read, SSRF).
xxe_injection_csharp.solution: Use DtdProcessing.Prohibit and set XmlResolver to null.
xxe_injection_csharp.benefit: Prevention of XXE attacks (OWASP A05, CWE-611, SCS0007).

command_injection_csharp.name: Command injection (C#)
command_injection_csharp.risk: Process.Start() with user input allows arbitrary OS command running.
command_injection_csharp.solution: Use ProcessStartInfo with ArgumentList. Validate and whitelist inputs.
command_injection_csharp.benefit: Prevention of OS command injection (OWASP A03, CWE-78, SCS0001).

weak_crypto_csharp.name: Weak cryptography (C#)
weak_crypto_csharp.risk: MD5, SHA1, DES, TripleDES and ECB mode are cryptographically broken.
weak_crypto_csharp.solution: Use SHA256, SHA512, or AES-GCM. For passwords, use BCrypt/Argon2/PBKDF2.
weak_crypto_csharp.benefit: Strong cryptographic operations (OWASP A02, CWE-328, SCS0006/CA5350).

weak_random_csharp.name: Weak random (C#)
weak_random_csharp.risk: System.Random is predictable — tokens, sessions, and keys generated with it can be guessed.
weak_random_csharp.solution: Use RandomNumberGenerator (System.Security.Cryptography) for security-sensitive random generation.
weak_random_csharp.benefit: Unpredictable token/key generation (OWASP A02, CWE-330, SCS0005).

ssl_bypass_csharp.name: SSL/TLS bypass (C#)
ssl_bypass_csharp.risk: ServerCertificateValidationCallback returning true disables certificate validation (MITM attack).
ssl_bypass_csharp.solution: Use default certificate validation. Never bypass SSL checks in production.
ssl_bypass_csharp.benefit: Secure TLS connections with proper certificate validation (OWASP A02, CWE-295, SCS0004).

xss_raw_html.name: XSS via Html.Raw()
xss_raw_html.risk: Html.Raw() outputs unescaped HTML, allowing cross-site scripting if user input is included.
xss_raw_html.solution: Use HtmlEncoder.Encode() or Razor auto-escaping (@Model.Value). Only use Html.Raw for trusted static content.
xss_raw_html.benefit: Prevention of XSS attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-79, SCS0029).

cors_permissive_csharp.name: Permissive CORS (C#)
cors_permissive_csharp.risk: AllowAnyOrigin() or WithOrigins("*") allows any domain to make authenticated requests.
cors_permissive_csharp.solution: Specify allowed origins matching your frontend domains with WithOrigins().
cors_permissive_csharp.benefit: Prevention of cross-origin data theft (OWASP A01, CWE-942).

open_redirect_csharp.name: Open redirect (C#)
open_redirect_csharp.risk: Redirect() with Request data allows phishing via trusted domain.
open_redirect_csharp.solution: Use Url.IsLocalUrl() to validate redirect URLs before redirecting.
open_redirect_csharp.benefit: Prevention of open redirect attacks (OWASP A01, CWE-601, SCS0027).

verbose_exception_csharp.name: Verbose exception (C#)
verbose_exception_csharp.risk: UseDeveloperExceptionPage() or exposed StackTrace reveals internal details to attackers.
verbose_exception_csharp.solution: Use UseExceptionHandler() in production. Never expose stack traces to users.
verbose_exception_csharp.benefit: Prevention of information disclosure (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

secret_logged_csharp.name: Secret logged (C#)
secret_logged_csharp.risk: Logging passwords, tokens, or API keys exposes secrets in log files and monitoring systems.
secret_logged_csharp.solution: Never log sensitive data. Use structured logging with placeholder values.
secret_logged_csharp.benefit: Secret protection in logs (OWASP A09, CWE-532).

ldap_injection_csharp.name: LDAP injection (C#)
ldap_injection_csharp.risk: String concatenation in DirectorySearcher.Filter allows LDAP injection attacks.
ldap_injection_csharp.solution: Use parameterized LDAP queries or escape special characters with LdapEncoder.
ldap_injection_csharp.benefit: Prevention of LDAP injection attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-90, SCS0026).

request_validation_disabled.name: Request validation disabled
request_validation_disabled.risk: [ValidateInput(false)] or validateRequest="false" disables built-in XSS/injection protection.
request_validation_disabled.solution: Keep request validation enabled. Use [AllowHtml] on specific properties if needed.
request_validation_disabled.benefit: Built-in protection against injection attacks (OWASP A03, SCS0017).

db_logic_controller_csharp.name: DB logic in controller (C#)
db_logic_controller_csharp.risk: DbContext/SqlCommand in Controller violates separation of concerns, making code untestable.
db_logic_controller_csharp.solution: Move database logic to Service or Repository classes. Controllers should only orchestrate.
db_logic_controller_csharp.benefit: Clean architecture with testable, maintainable layers.

console_write_csharp.name: Console.Write in production (C#)
console_write_csharp.risk: Console.WriteLine bypasses logging framework — no log levels, no rotation, no monitoring.
console_write_csharp.solution: Use ILogger with appropriate log levels (LogDebug, LogInformation, LogWarning, LogError).
console_write_csharp.benefit: Structured, configurable logging with proper monitoring integration.

catch_all_exception_csharp.name: Generic catch (C#)
catch_all_exception_csharp.risk: catch(Exception) swallows all exceptions including runtime errors, hiding bugs.
catch_all_exception_csharp.solution: Catch specific exception types (InvalidOperationException, IOException, etc.).
catch_all_exception_csharp.benefit: Precise error handling, no hidden failures (CWE-396).

cs_too_many_params.name: Too many C# method parameters (6+)
cs_too_many_params.risk: A method or constructor with 6 or more parameters is hard to call correctly, hard to test, and often violates the Single Responsibility Principle (SonarQube S107).
cs_too_many_params.solution: Group related parameters into a dedicated record, class, or value object.
cs_too_many_params.benefit: Simpler method signatures, easier testing, better alignment with the Single Responsibility Principle.

cs_deep_nesting.name: Excessive nesting depth (C#, 6+ levels)
cs_deep_nesting.risk: Code nested more than 5 levels deep is extremely difficult to read, test, and maintain (SonarQube S3776).
cs_deep_nesting.solution: Apply early return / guard clauses. Extract nested logic into dedicated private methods.
cs_deep_nesting.benefit: Linear code is easier to understand, test, and modify than deeply nested pyramids.

cs_empty_catch_block.name: Empty catch block (C#)
cs_empty_catch_block.risk: An empty catch block silently swallows exceptions. Bugs become impossible to diagnose in production (SonarQube S2486).
cs_empty_catch_block.solution: At minimum, log the exception with ILogger. Prefer propagating or rethrowing the exception.
cs_empty_catch_block.benefit: Every error is visible and traceable — production debugging becomes possible.

cs_magic_number.name: Magic number in comparison (C#)
cs_magic_number.risk: Comparing directly to unexplained numeric literals makes the code hard to understand and maintain (SonarQube S109).
cs_magic_number.solution: Extract the numeric literal into a named constant, e.g. const int HttpNotFound = 404.
cs_magic_number.benefit: Self-documenting code — the intent behind each numeric value is explicit and changeable in one place.

cs_high_coupling.name: High coupling — too many C# interfaces (SonarQube S1200)
cs_high_coupling.risk: A class implementing more than 5 interfaces and base classes has extremely high coupling. This makes testing, mocking, and changing any dependency difficult.
cs_high_coupling.solution: Apply the Interface Segregation Principle. Split large interfaces into smaller, focused ones.
cs_high_coupling.benefit: Low-coupled classes are easier to test in isolation and change without side effects.

cs_string_format_legacy.name: string.Format() instead of interpolation (C#)
cs_string_format_legacy.risk: string.Format() is verbose, error-prone (wrong argument count causes runtime exceptions), and harder to read than string interpolation.
cs_string_format_legacy.solution: Replace string.Format("Hello {0}", name) with the interpolation syntax $"Hello {name}". String interpolation is type-safe and checked at compile time.
cs_string_format_legacy.benefit: String interpolation is safer, more readable, and performs better than string.Format in most scenarios.

sql_injection_concat_php.name: SQL injection (PHP concatenation)
sql_injection_concat_php.risk: String concatenation in mysqli_query/DB::raw allows SQL injection.
sql_injection_concat_php.solution: Use prepared statements with PDO or parameterized queries.
sql_injection_concat_php.benefit: Immunity against SQL injection attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

command_injection_php.name: Command injection (PHP)
command_injection_php.risk: shell_exec/system/passthru/popen with user input allows arbitrary OS command running.
command_injection_php.solution: Use escapeshellarg()/escapeshellcmd() or Symfony Process component with argument list.
command_injection_php.benefit: Prevention of OS command injection (OWASP A03, CWE-78).

eval_injection_php.name: Code injection (PHP)
eval_injection_php.risk: Dynamic code evaluation allows arbitrary PHP code running.
eval_injection_php.solution: Avoid dynamic evaluation entirely. Use closures, call_user_func, or configuration-based logic.
eval_injection_php.benefit: Prevention of remote code running (OWASP A03, CWE-94).

unsafe_deserialization_php.name: Unsafe deserialization (PHP)
unsafe_deserialization_php.risk: unserialize() with untrusted data allows PHP Object Injection attacks.
unsafe_deserialization_php.solution: Use json_decode() instead. If unserialize is required, use allowed_classes option.
unsafe_deserialization_php.benefit: Protection against object injection attacks (OWASP A08, CWE-502).

file_inclusion_php.name: File inclusion (PHP)
file_inclusion_php.risk: include/require with user-controlled variable allows Local/Remote File Inclusion (LFI/RFI).
file_inclusion_php.solution: Use a whitelist of allowed templates. Never pass user input to include/require.
file_inclusion_php.benefit: Prevention of file inclusion attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-98).

xxe_injection_php.name: XXE injection (PHP)
xxe_injection_php.risk: simplexml_load_string/file without libxml_disable_entity_loader allows XXE attacks.
xxe_injection_php.solution: Call libxml_disable_entity_loader(true) before parsing XML. Use LIBXML_NOENT flag.
xxe_injection_php.benefit: Prevention of XXE attacks (OWASP A05, CWE-611).

xss_echo_php.name: XSS via echo (PHP)
xss_echo_php.risk: Echoing $_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST without escaping allows cross-site scripting.
xss_echo_php.solution: Use htmlspecialchars($var, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') for all user output.
xss_echo_php.benefit: Prevention of XSS attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-79).

xss_blade_unescaped.name: XSS via unescaped Blade output
xss_blade_unescaped.risk: {!! $var !!} outputs unescaped HTML in Laravel Blade, allowing XSS if user input is included.
xss_blade_unescaped.solution: Use {{ $var }} (auto-escaped) instead of {!! !!}. Only use {!! !!} for trusted static HTML.
xss_blade_unescaped.benefit: Prevention of XSS via Blade templates (OWASP A03, CWE-79).

xss_react_dangerous.name: XSS via React dangerouslySetInnerHTML
xss_react_dangerous.risk: dangerouslySetInnerHTML injects raw HTML into the DOM, allowing XSS if user input is not sanitized.
xss_react_dangerous.solution: Sanitize content with DOMPurify before injection, or use React's default JSX escaping.
xss_react_dangerous.benefit: Prevention of XSS in React components (OWASP A03, CWE-79).

xss_angular_bypass.name: XSS via Angular security bypass
xss_angular_bypass.risk: bypassSecurityTrustHtml/Script/Url disables Angular's built-in XSS protection for the given value.
xss_angular_bypass.solution: Avoid bypassSecurityTrust* methods. Use Angular's sanitization pipeline or DomSanitizer.sanitize().
xss_angular_bypass.benefit: Prevention of XSS by maintaining Angular's security model (OWASP A03, CWE-79).

xss_vue_vhtml.name: XSS via Vue.js v-html directive
xss_vue_vhtml.risk: v-html renders raw HTML in the DOM, allowing XSS if user-controlled data is bound.
xss_vue_vhtml.solution: Use text interpolation {{ }} instead of v-html. If HTML is needed, sanitize with DOMPurify first.
xss_vue_vhtml.benefit: Prevention of XSS in Vue.js templates (OWASP A03, CWE-79).

xss_svelte_html.name: XSS via Svelte {@html} tag
xss_svelte_html.risk: {@html} renders raw HTML without escaping, allowing XSS if the content includes user input.
xss_svelte_html.solution: Avoid {@html} with user input. Sanitize content with DOMPurify before using {@html}.
xss_svelte_html.benefit: Prevention of XSS in Svelte components (OWASP A03, CWE-79).

sql_injection_django_raw.name: SQL injection via Django raw SQL
sql_injection_django_raw.risk: cursor.execute()/raw()/extra()/RawSQL() with string concatenation allows SQL injection.
sql_injection_django_raw.solution: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('... WHERE x = %s', [val]) or Django ORM querysets.
sql_injection_django_raw.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in Django applications (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_sqlalchemy_text.name: SQL injection via SQLAlchemy text()
sql_injection_sqlalchemy_text.risk: text() with string concatenation bypasses SQLAlchemy's parameterization, enabling SQL injection.
sql_injection_sqlalchemy_text.solution: Use bound parameters: text('... WHERE x = :val').bindparams(val=user_input).
sql_injection_sqlalchemy_text.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in SQLAlchemy queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_jpa_native.name: SQL injection via JPA/Hibernate native query
sql_injection_jpa_native.risk: createNativeQuery()/createQuery() with string concatenation allows SQL injection.
sql_injection_jpa_native.solution: Use named parameters: createQuery('... WHERE x = :val').setParameter('val', input).
sql_injection_jpa_native.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in JPA/Hibernate applications (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_mybatis.name: SQL injection via MyBatis ${} interpolation
sql_injection_mybatis.risk: ${} in MyBatis annotations performs string interpolation (not parameterization), enabling SQL injection.
sql_injection_mybatis.solution: Use #{} instead of ${} for parameter binding. ${} should only be used for table/column names.
sql_injection_mybatis.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in MyBatis queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_dapper.name: SQL injection via Dapper raw query
sql_injection_dapper.risk: Execute()/Query() with string concatenation bypasses Dapper's parameterization.
sql_injection_dapper.solution: Use parameterized queries: Query('... WHERE x = @Val', new { Val = input }).
sql_injection_dapper.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in Dapper queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_whereraw_php.name: SQL injection via Laravel whereRaw/havingRaw
sql_injection_whereraw_php.risk: whereRaw()/havingRaw()/selectRaw() with concatenation bypasses Eloquent's query builder protection.
sql_injection_whereraw_php.solution: Use bindings: whereRaw('col = ?', [$val]) or Eloquent methods: where('col', $val).
sql_injection_whereraw_php.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in Laravel Eloquent (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_wpdb.name: SQL injection via WordPress $wpdb
sql_injection_wpdb.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in WordPress database queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_doctrine.name: SQL injection via Doctrine DQL
sql_injection_doctrine.risk: createQuery() with string concatenation in DQL enables SQL injection.
sql_injection_doctrine.solution: Use bound parameters: createQuery('... WHERE x = :val')->setParameter('val', $input).
sql_injection_doctrine.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in Doctrine ORM queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_sequelize.name: SQL injection via Sequelize raw query
sql_injection_sequelize.risk: sequelize.query() with string concatenation bypasses Sequelize's parameterization.
sql_injection_sequelize.solution: Use replacements: sequelize.query('... WHERE x = ?', { replacements: [val] }).
sql_injection_sequelize.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in Sequelize queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

nosql_injection_mongoose.name: NoSQL injection via Mongoose $where
nosql_injection_mongoose.risk: $where operator executes JavaScript on the server, enabling NoSQL injection if user input is included.
nosql_injection_mongoose.solution: Avoid $where with user input. Use standard Mongoose query operators ({field: value}).
nosql_injection_mongoose.benefit: Prevention of NoSQL injection in MongoDB/Mongoose (OWASP A03, CWE-943).

sql_injection_prisma.name: SQL injection via Prisma $queryRaw
sql_injection_prisma.risk: $queryRaw/$executeRaw with string concatenation bypasses Prisma's type-safe query builder.
sql_injection_prisma.solution: Use Prisma's tagged template: prisma.$queryRaw`... WHERE x = ${val}` (auto-parameterized).
sql_injection_prisma.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in Prisma queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_injection_typeorm.name: SQL injection via TypeORM raw query
sql_injection_typeorm.risk: connection.query() with string concatenation allows SQL injection.
sql_injection_typeorm.solution: Use parameterized queries: query('... WHERE x = $1', [val]) or TypeORM QueryBuilder.
sql_injection_typeorm.benefit: Prevention of SQL injection in TypeORM queries (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

ssrf_python.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (Python)
ssrf_python.risk: HTTP requests with user-controlled URLs allow attackers to access internal services and cloud metadata (OWASP A10, CWE-918).
ssrf_python.solution: Validate and allowlist target URLs/domains. Block private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x).
ssrf_python.benefit: Prevention of SSRF attacks targeting internal infrastructure.

ssrf_java.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (Java)
ssrf_java.risk: URL connections with user-controlled input allow attackers to probe internal services (OWASP A10, CWE-918).
ssrf_java.solution: Validate URLs against an allowlist. Use java.net.URI to parse and verify hostname before connecting.
ssrf_java.benefit: Prevention of SSRF attacks in Java applications.

ssrf_csharp.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (C#)
ssrf_csharp.risk: HttpClient requests with user-controlled URLs allow SSRF attacks (OWASP A10, CWE-918).
ssrf_csharp.solution: Validate and allowlist target URLs. Use Uri.TryCreate() to parse and verify hostname.
ssrf_csharp.benefit: Prevention of SSRF attacks in .NET applications.

ssrf_php.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (PHP)
ssrf_php.risk: file_get_contents()/curl with user-controlled URLs allow SSRF attacks (OWASP A10, CWE-918).
ssrf_php.solution: Validate URLs against an allowlist. Use parse_url() and block private IP ranges.
ssrf_php.benefit: Prevention of SSRF attacks in PHP applications.

ssrf_javascript.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (JavaScript)
ssrf_javascript.risk: fetch()/axios with user-controlled URLs allow SSRF attacks (OWASP A10, CWE-918).
ssrf_javascript.solution: Validate and allowlist target URLs/domains before making HTTP requests.
ssrf_javascript.benefit: Prevention of SSRF attacks in Node.js applications.

path_traversal_python.name: Path traversal (Python)
path_traversal_python.risk: User-controlled file paths allow reading/writing arbitrary files on the server (CWE-22, OWASP A01).
path_traversal_python.solution: Validate paths with os.path.realpath() and verify they stay within the allowed base directory.
path_traversal_python.benefit: Prevention of directory traversal and unauthorized file access.

path_traversal_java.name: Path traversal (Java)
path_traversal_java.risk: File operations with user-controlled paths allow directory traversal attacks (CWE-22, OWASP A01).
path_traversal_java.solution: Use Path.normalize().startsWith(basePath) to validate resolved paths stay within bounds.
path_traversal_java.benefit: Prevention of path traversal attacks in Java applications.

path_traversal_csharp.name: Path traversal (C#)
path_traversal_csharp.risk: File.Read/Write with user-controlled paths allow directory traversal attacks (CWE-22, OWASP A01).
path_traversal_csharp.solution: Use Path.GetFullPath() and verify the resolved path starts with the allowed base directory.
path_traversal_csharp.benefit: Prevention of path traversal attacks in .NET applications.

path_traversal_javascript.name: Path traversal (JavaScript)
path_traversal_javascript.risk: fs operations with user-controlled paths allow directory traversal attacks (CWE-22, OWASP A01).
path_traversal_javascript.solution: Use path.resolve() and verify the result starts with the allowed base directory.
path_traversal_javascript.benefit: Prevention of path traversal attacks in Node.js applications.

django_csrf_exempt.name: @csrf_exempt decorator (Django)
django_csrf_exempt.risk: Disabling CSRF protection exposes endpoints to cross-site request forgery attacks (CWE-352, OWASP A01).
django_csrf_exempt.solution: Remove @csrf_exempt and use Django's CSRF middleware. For APIs, use token-based authentication.
django_csrf_exempt.benefit: Full CSRF protection on all endpoints.

django_debug_enabled.name: DEBUG = True (Django)
django_debug_enabled.risk: Debug mode in production exposes stack traces, SQL queries, and sensitive configuration (CWE-489, OWASP A05).
django_debug_enabled.solution: Set DEBUG = False in production settings. Use environment variables: DEBUG = os.environ.get('DEBUG', 'False') == 'True'.
django_debug_enabled.benefit: No sensitive information leakage in production.

django_secret_key_weak.name: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY (Django)
django_secret_key_weak.risk: A hardcoded or weak SECRET_KEY compromises session signing, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens (CWE-798, OWASP A02).
django_secret_key_weak.solution: Load SECRET_KEY from environment variable: SECRET_KEY = os.environ['DJANGO_SECRET_KEY']. Generate with django.core.management.utils.get_random_secret_key().

flask_debug_enabled.name: Debug mode enabled (Flask)
flask_debug_enabled.risk: Flask debug mode enables the Werkzeug debugger, allowing remote code execution via the debug console (CWE-489, OWASP A05).
flask_debug_enabled.solution: Never use debug=True in production. Use environment variable: app.run(debug=os.environ.get('FLASK_DEBUG', 'False') == 'True').
flask_debug_enabled.benefit: No interactive debugger exposed in production.

flask_secret_key_weak.name: Hardcoded secret_key (Flask)
flask_secret_key_weak.risk: A hardcoded secret_key compromises session cookies and CSRF protection (CWE-798, OWASP A02).
flask_secret_key_weak.solution: Load from environment: app.secret_key = os.environ['FLASK_SECRET_KEY']. Generate with os.urandom(32).hex().

express_no_helmet.name: Missing Helmet middleware (Express)
express_no_helmet.risk: Without Helmet, Express apps lack security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, etc.), increasing attack surface (OWASP A05).
express_no_helmet.solution: Install and use Helmet: npm install helmet, then app.use(helmet()).
express_no_helmet.benefit: Security headers automatically set on all responses.

express_cors_wildcard.name: Permissive CORS configuration (Express)
express_cors_wildcard.risk: cors() without origin restriction or origin: '*' allows any website to make authenticated requests (CWE-942, OWASP A01).
express_cors_wildcard.benefit: Cross-origin requests restricted to trusted domains only.

insecure_cookie.name: Insecure cookie (missing HttpOnly/Secure)
insecure_cookie.risk: Cookies without HttpOnly are accessible via JavaScript (XSS). Without Secure, they are sent over unencrypted HTTP (CWE-614, OWASP A05).
insecure_cookie.solution: Always set HttpOnly=True and Secure=True on session and authentication cookies.
insecure_cookie.benefit: Cookies protected against XSS theft and network interception.

insecure_cookie_no_secure.name: Cookie without Secure flag
insecure_cookie_no_secure.risk: Cookies with secure=False are transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, allowing interception (CWE-614, OWASP A05).
insecure_cookie_no_secure.solution: Set secure=True on all cookies containing sensitive data.
insecure_cookie_no_secure.benefit: Cookie only sent over HTTPS, preventing network interception.

ldap_injection_python.name: LDAP injection (Python)
ldap_injection_python.risk: String concatenation in LDAP filters allows attackers to modify queries and bypass authentication (CWE-90, OWASP A03).
ldap_injection_python.solution: Use parameterized LDAP filters with ldap.filter.filter_format() or escape user input with ldap.filter.escape_filter_chars().
ldap_injection_python.benefit: LDAP queries safe from injection attacks.

ldap_injection_java.name: LDAP injection (Java)
ldap_injection_java.risk: String concatenation in LDAP search filters allows query manipulation and authentication bypass (CWE-90, OWASP A03).
ldap_injection_java.solution: Use parameterized searches with SearchControls or escape input with LdapEncoder.filterEncode().
ldap_injection_java.benefit: LDAP queries safe from injection attacks.

weak_crypto_php.name: Weak cryptography (PHP)
weak_crypto_php.risk: md5()/sha1() are cryptographically broken — vulnerable to collision and rainbow table attacks.
weak_crypto_php.solution: Use password_hash() with PASSWORD_BCRYPT or PASSWORD_ARGON2ID for passwords.

weak_random_php.name: Weak random (PHP)
weak_random_php.risk: rand()/mt_rand() are predictable — tokens and keys generated with them can be guessed.
weak_random_php.solution: Use random_bytes() or random_int() for security-sensitive random generation.

open_redirect_php.name: Open redirect (PHP)
open_redirect_php.risk: header('Location: '.$_GET[...]) allows phishing via trusted domain.
open_redirect_php.solution: Validate redirect URLs against a whitelist of allowed paths/domains.
open_redirect_php.benefit: Prevention of open redirect attacks (OWASP A01, CWE-601).

extract_usage_php.name: Variable overwrite (PHP extract)
extract_usage_php.risk: extract($_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST) overwrites local variables, enabling injection attacks.
extract_usage_php.solution: Access superglobals directly or use array destructuring. Never extract untrusted data.
extract_usage_php.benefit: Prevention of variable injection attacks (OWASP A03, CWE-621).

type_juggling_php.name: Type juggling (PHP)
type_juggling_php.risk: Loose comparison (==) in auth context allows bypass via PHP type coercion.
type_juggling_php.solution: Use strict comparison (===) or hash_equals() for security-sensitive comparisons.
type_juggling_php.benefit: Prevention of authentication bypass (OWASP A07, CWE-1024).

mass_assignment_laravel.name: Mass assignment (Laravel)
mass_assignment_laravel.risk: $request->all() in create()/update() allows users to set any database column.
mass_assignment_laravel.benefit: Prevention of mass assignment attacks (OWASP A01, CWE-915).

password_reversible_storage_python.name: Reversible password storage (Python)
password_reversible_storage_python.risk: A password is encrypted with a reversible algorithm (base64, Fernet, AES) instead of a one-way hash. Compromise of the encryption key exposes all stored passwords (CWE-257).
password_reversible_storage_python.solution: Use bcrypt, Argon2id, or scrypt. Libraries: bcrypt, argon2-cffi, passlib.
password_reversible_storage_python.benefit: Stored passwords cannot be recovered even after a database breach (OWASP A02, CWE-257).

password_reversible_storage_java.name: Reversible password storage (Java)
password_reversible_storage_java.risk: A symmetric cipher (AES, DES, Blowfish) is used to store a password. Reversible encryption can be undone if the key is compromised (CWE-257).
password_reversible_storage_java.solution: Use BCrypt, PBKDF2, or Argon2. In Java: BCryptPasswordEncoder (Spring Security) or jBCrypt.
password_reversible_storage_java.benefit: One-way hashing makes stored passwords practically irrecoverable after a breach (OWASP A02, CWE-257).

db_error_exposed_python.name: DB error exposed in response (Python)
db_error_exposed_python.risk: A database exception message is returned in the HTTP response, revealing table names, SQL queries, or stack traces (CWE-209).
db_error_exposed_python.solution: Return a generic error message to the client. Log the detailed exception server-side with a logging framework.
db_error_exposed_python.benefit: Prevents database reconnaissance and targeted injection attacks (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

db_error_exposed_php.name: DB error exposed in response (PHP)
db_error_exposed_php.risk: A database exception is echoed to the HTTP response, revealing internal details that assist attackers in mapping the database structure (CWE-209).
db_error_exposed_php.solution: Set display_errors=Off in production php.ini. Log exceptions with Monolog or PSR-3. Return a generic message.
db_error_exposed_php.benefit: Prevents information disclosure enabling targeted injection attacks (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

mass_assignment_python.name: Mass assignment (Python)
mass_assignment_python.risk: Passing **request.POST or **request.json to a model constructor allows users to set any attribute, including role, is_admin, or balance (CWE-915).
mass_assignment_python.solution: Whitelist allowed fields via a form (Django ModelForm, DRF Serializer) or explicit key extraction.
mass_assignment_python.benefit: Prevents privilege escalation and data integrity violations (OWASP A01, CWE-915).

mass_assignment_js.name: Mass assignment (JavaScript)
mass_assignment_js.risk: Passing req.body directly to Model.create() or a model constructor allows injection of any field, including sensitive ones like role or isAdmin (CWE-915).
mass_assignment_js.solution: Explicitly pick only the allowed fields: const { name, email } = req.body; await User.create({ name, email });
mass_assignment_js.benefit: Prevents privilege escalation attacks on database records (OWASP A01, CWE-915).

db_tls_disabled_python.name: DB connection without TLS (Python)
db_tls_disabled_python.risk: The database connection has TLS disabled or certificate validation bypassed. All traffic is transmitted in cleartext and can be intercepted (CWE-327).
db_tls_disabled_python.solution: Enable TLS: sslmode=require or sslmode=verify-full (psycopg2), tls=True with tlsCAFile (pymongo), ?sslmode=require in SQLAlchemy URL.
db_tls_disabled_python.benefit: Encrypts all data in transit between the application and the database (OWASP A02, CWE-327).

db_tls_disabled_js.name: DB connection without TLS (JavaScript)
db_tls_disabled_js.risk: TLS is disabled or certificate validation is bypassed for a database connection. All traffic is sent in cleartext, exposing it to network interception (CWE-327).
db_tls_disabled_js.solution: Set ssl: true and rejectUnauthorized: true. Provide a valid CA certificate. For pg: { ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: '...' } }.
db_tls_disabled_js.benefit: Encrypts all database communications and verifies server identity (OWASP A02, CWE-327).

verbose_exception_php.name: Verbose exception (PHP)
verbose_exception_php.risk: var_dump()/print_r()/debug_backtrace() expose internal details to attackers.
verbose_exception_php.solution: Use a logging framework. Set display_errors=Off in production php.ini.
verbose_exception_php.benefit: Prevention of information disclosure (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

secret_logged_php.name: Secret logged (PHP)
secret_logged_php.risk: Logging passwords, tokens, or API keys exposes secrets in log files.
