secret_logged_php.solution: Never log sensitive data. Use placeholder values or mask secrets before logging.
secret_logged_php.benefit: Secret protection in logs (OWASP A09, CWE-532).

db_logic_controller_php.name: DB logic in controller (PHP)
db_logic_controller_php.risk: DB::/->query() in Controller violates separation of concerns, making code untestable.
db_logic_controller_php.solution: Move database logic to Repository or Service classes. Controllers should only orchestrate.
db_logic_controller_php.benefit: Clean architecture with testable, maintainable layers.

error_suppressor_php.name: Error suppressor (PHP @)
error_suppressor_php.risk: @ operator silences errors, hiding bugs and security issues.
error_suppressor_php.solution: Handle errors explicitly with try/catch or error checking. Configure error_reporting properly.
error_suppressor_php.benefit: Visible errors, easier debugging, no hidden failures.

catch_all_exception_php.name: Generic catch (PHP)
catch_all_exception_php.risk: catch(\Exception) swallows all exceptions including runtime errors, hiding bugs.
catch_all_exception_php.benefit: Precise error handling, no hidden failures (CWE-396).

php_too_many_params.name: Too many PHP function parameters (6+)
php_too_many_params.risk: A function or method with 6 or more parameters is hard to call correctly, hard to test, and often violates the Single Responsibility Principle.
php_too_many_params.solution: Group related parameters into a dedicated array, DTO, or value object.
php_too_many_params.benefit: Simpler function signatures, easier testing, better alignment with the Single Responsibility Principle.

php_deep_nesting.name: Excessive nesting depth (PHP, 6+ levels)
php_deep_nesting.risk: Code nested more than 5 levels deep is extremely difficult to read, test, and maintain.
php_deep_nesting.solution: Apply early return / guard clauses. Extract nested logic into dedicated private methods.
php_deep_nesting.benefit: Linear code is easier to understand, test, and modify than deeply nested pyramids.

php_empty_catch_block.name: Empty catch block (PHP)
php_empty_catch_block.risk: An empty catch block silently swallows exceptions. Bugs become impossible to diagnose in production.
php_empty_catch_block.solution: At minimum, log the exception. Prefer propagating or rethrowing the exception.
php_empty_catch_block.benefit: Every error is visible and traceable — production debugging becomes possible.

php_public_property.name: Non-constant public property (PHP)
php_public_property.risk: A public property exposes the internal state of a class, breaking encapsulation. Any code can read or modify it directly.
php_public_property.solution: Make the property private and provide getter/setter methods. For read-only properties, use PHP 8.1+ readonly.
php_public_property.benefit: Proper encapsulation allows internal implementation changes without breaking client code.

php_string_concat_loop.name: String concatenation in loop (PHP)
php_string_concat_loop.risk: Concatenating strings with .= inside a loop creates a new string on every iteration, degrading performance for large arrays.
php_string_concat_loop.solution: Collect values in an array and use implode() at the end.
php_string_concat_loop.benefit: implode() is O(n) and allocates memory only once — much faster than iterative concatenation.

php_exit_die.name: Use of exit()/die() in PHP
php_exit_die.risk: Calling exit() or die() in production code terminates the PHP process abruptly, bypassing shutdown handlers and framework cleanup code. It makes testing impossible.
php_exit_die.solution: Throw an exception instead. In controllers, return an appropriate HTTP response. Reserve exit() for CLI entry points only.
php_exit_die.benefit: Code that throws exceptions is testable, framework-compatible, and allows proper error handling at higher levels.

missing_mfa_python.name: Missing MFA (Python)
missing_mfa_python.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_python.solution: Integrate pyotp or django-otp for TOTP-based two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_python.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_java.name: Missing MFA (Java)
missing_mfa_java.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_java.solution: Integrate a TOTP library (dev.samstevens.totp, Google Authenticator) for two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_java.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_csharp.name: Missing MFA (C#)
missing_mfa_csharp.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_csharp.solution: Enable ASP.NET Identity TwoFactorSignInAsync or integrate a TOTP library.
missing_mfa_csharp.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_javascript.name: Missing MFA (JavaScript)
missing_mfa_javascript.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_javascript.solution: Integrate speakeasy or otplib for TOTP-based two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_javascript.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

missing_mfa_php.name: Missing MFA (PHP)
missing_mfa_php.risk: Authentication without multi-factor authentication exposes accounts to credential theft (CWE-308).
missing_mfa_php.solution: Integrate google2fa or pragmarx/google2fa-laravel for TOTP-based two-factor authentication.
missing_mfa_php.benefit: Stronger authentication, reduced risk of account compromise.

pii_logged.name: PII Logged
pii_logged.risk: Personally identifiable information (email, phone, address, SSN) written to logs violates GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) and risks data breach via log exposure (CWE-532).
pii_logged.solution: Replace PII with anonymized identifiers (user ID, hashed values) in all log statements.
pii_logged.benefit: GDPR compliance, reduced data breach surface in log infrastructure.

missing_data_retention.name: Missing Data Retention
missing_data_retention.risk: Personal data stored without deletion or anonymization logic violates GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation principle.
missing_data_retention.solution: Implement delete/purge/anonymize methods on data models containing personal information.
missing_data_retention.benefit: GDPR compliance, reduced legal exposure, right to erasure (Art. 17) support.

dockerfile_root_user.name: Dockerfile runs as root
dockerfile_root_user.risk: Container runs as root user by default, increasing blast radius if compromised (CWE-250).
dockerfile_root_user.solution: Add a USER directive with a non-root user (e.g., USER appuser) after installing dependencies.
dockerfile_root_user.benefit: Principle of least privilege, reduced container escape risk.

dockerfile_unpinned_base.name: Unpinned base image
dockerfile_unpinned_base.risk: Base image without version tag (FROM node) pulls latest, causing non-reproducible builds and potential supply chain issues.
dockerfile_unpinned_base.solution: Pin base image to a specific version or digest (e.g., FROM node:20-alpine or FROM node@sha256:...).
dockerfile_unpinned_base.benefit: Reproducible builds, protection against supply chain attacks.

dockerfile_copy_all.name: COPY . . in Dockerfile
dockerfile_copy_all.risk: COPY . . copies the entire build context including potential secrets (.env, credentials, SSH keys).
dockerfile_copy_all.solution: Use a .dockerignore file and copy only required files/directories explicitly.
dockerfile_copy_all.benefit: Smaller image, no accidental secret exposure in container layers.

deprecated_api_java.name: Deprecated API (Java)
deprecated_api_java.risk: Deprecated methods (Thread.stop, finalize, new Date(y,m,d)) may be removed in future JDK versions and have known issues.
deprecated_api_java.solution: Replace with modern alternatives: Thread.interrupt(), try-with-resources, java.time API.
deprecated_api_java.benefit: Future-proof code, better reliability and compatibility.

deprecated_api_csharp.name: Deprecated API (C#)
deprecated_api_csharp.risk: Deprecated classes (BinaryFormatter, WebClient, SHA1Managed) have known security or performance issues.
deprecated_api_csharp.solution: Replace with System.Text.Json, HttpClient, SHA256 from System.Security.Cryptography.
deprecated_api_csharp.benefit: Secure serialization, modern HTTP stack, strong hashing.

deprecated_api_php.name: Deprecated API (PHP)
deprecated_api_php.risk: Removed functions (mysql_*, ereg, each, create_function) are unavailable since PHP 7+/8+.
deprecated_api_php.solution: Replace with PDO/mysqli, preg_match, foreach, anonymous functions.
deprecated_api_php.benefit: PHP 8+ compatibility, improved security and performance.

deprecated_api_javascript.name: Deprecated API (JavaScript)
deprecated_api_javascript.risk: Deprecated features (escape, __proto__) cause performance issues and security risks.
deprecated_api_javascript.solution: Replace with DOM API, encodeURIComponent, Object.setPrototypeOf.
deprecated_api_javascript.benefit: Modern standards compliance, better performance and security.

privilege_escalation.name: Privilege Escalation
privilege_escalation.risk: Code uses os.setuid(0), subprocess with sudo/su, escalating privileges to root (CWE-250).
privilege_escalation.solution: Run processes with minimal privileges. Use capability-based access instead of root.
privilege_escalation.benefit: Least privilege principle enforced, reduced blast radius on compromise.

unencrypted_transfer.name: Unencrypted Data Transfer
unencrypted_transfer.risk: Data sent via plain FTP or SMTP without TLS, exposing credentials and content in transit (CWE-319).
unencrypted_transfer.solution: Use FTP_TLS (FTPS) or SFTP for file transfers, SMTP with STARTTLS or SMTP_SSL for emails.
unencrypted_transfer.benefit: Data confidentiality in transit, compliance with ISO 27001 A.5.14.

missing_auth_decorator.name: Missing Authentication Decorator
missing_auth_decorator.risk: Sensitive route (admin, API delete/update) lacks authentication decorator, accessible without login (CWE-306).
missing_auth_decorator.solution: Add @login_required, @auth_required or equivalent decorator on all sensitive routes.
missing_auth_decorator.benefit: Access control enforced, prevents unauthorized access to critical endpoints.

pii_in_tests.name: PII in Test Code
pii_in_tests.risk: Real personal data (emails, phone numbers) hardcoded in tests risks exposure in CI logs and repos (CWE-359).
pii_in_tests.solution: Use anonymized test data (@example.com, +33600000000) or factory libraries (Faker).
pii_in_tests.benefit: GDPR compliance, no risk of personal data leakage from test infrastructure.

insecure_cloud_config.name: Insecure Cloud Configuration
insecure_cloud_config.risk: Cloud resource configured with public access (S3 public-read, SG 0.0.0.0/0, RDS publicly accessible) (CWE-284).
insecure_cloud_config.solution: Set private ACLs, restrict security groups to specific CIDRs, disable public access on databases.
insecure_cloud_config.benefit: Cloud resources protected from unauthorized access, reduced attack surface.

unbounded_query.name: Unbounded Query
unbounded_query.risk: Database query without LIMIT or pagination can return millions of rows, causing OOM or denial of service (CWE-770).
unbounded_query.solution: Add LIMIT clause, use pagination (offset/limit or cursor), or slice ORM querysets.
unbounded_query.benefit: Predictable memory usage, application stability under load.

missing_monitoring.name: Missing Monitoring/Logging
missing_monitoring.risk: API endpoints without logging prevent incident detection and forensic analysis (CWE-778).
missing_monitoring.solution: Add logging module import and log critical operations (authentication, data changes, errors).
missing_monitoring.benefit: Security event visibility, faster incident response, audit trail compliance.

missing_security_docs.name: Undocumented Security Function
missing_security_docs.risk: Security-critical function (encrypt, hash, authenticate, sanitize) without docstring hampers review and maintenance.
missing_security_docs.solution: Add a docstring explaining the algorithm, parameters, return values, and security assumptions.
missing_security_docs.benefit: Easier security review, reduced risk of misuse by other developers.

missing_change_management.name: Missing Change Management
missing_change_management.risk: Direct force-push or schema changes (ALTER/DROP TABLE) without migration system bypasses change control (CWE-439).
missing_change_management.solution: Use migration tools (Alembic, Flyway), CI/CD pipelines, and protected branches.
missing_change_management.benefit: Auditable change history, rollback capability, team coordination.

insecure_local_storage.name: Insecure Local Storage
insecure_local_storage.risk: Sensitive data (tokens, passwords, API keys) stored in localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript on the page, including XSS payloads (CWE-922).
insecure_local_storage.solution: Use httpOnly secure cookies for authentication tokens. Use sessionStorage or in-memory storage for short-lived sensitive data.
insecure_local_storage.benefit: Sensitive data protected from XSS-based theft, reduced session hijacking risk.

destructive_without_backup.name: Destructive Operation Without Backup
destructive_without_backup.risk: DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE or DELETE without WHERE performed outside migration tools — risks irreversible data loss without rollback capability (CWE-400).
destructive_without_backup.solution: Use migration tools (Alembic, Flyway, Django migrations) for schema changes. Always include WHERE clause in DELETE statements.
destructive_without_backup.benefit: Data integrity preserved, rollback capability maintained, audit trail for destructive operations.

js_debugger_statement.name: Debugger statement in production (JavaScript)
js_debugger_statement.risk: A debugger statement left in production code indicates incomplete cleanup and can cause unexpected pauses for developers with DevTools open.
js_debugger_statement.solution: Remove all debugger statements before deploying to production. Use proper logging frameworks or DevTools breakpoints via source maps instead.
js_debugger_statement.benefit: Clean production code without debug artifacts — no unintended pauses for developers with DevTools open.

js_no_var.name: Use of var keyword (JavaScript)
js_no_var.risk: The var keyword creates function-scoped variables that are hoisted, leading to surprising behaviors like using variables before they are declared.
js_no_var.solution: Replace var with const for values that do not change, or let for values that need to be reassigned.
js_no_var.benefit: Block-scoped variables (let/const) make code behavior predictable and easier to reason about.

js_too_many_params.name: Too many JavaScript function parameters (6+)
js_too_many_params.risk: A function with 6 or more parameters is hard to call correctly, hard to test, and often indicates a violation of the Single Responsibility Principle.
js_too_many_params.solution: Group related parameters into an options object (destructured).
js_too_many_params.benefit: Options objects are self-documenting, allow optional parameters easily, and are more readable at the call site.

js_empty_catch_block.name: Empty catch block (JavaScript)
js_empty_catch_block.risk: An empty catch block silently swallows exceptions. Bugs become impossible to diagnose in production.
js_empty_catch_block.solution: At minimum, log the error to the console or a monitoring system.
js_empty_catch_block.benefit: Every error is visible and traceable — production debugging becomes possible.

js_deep_nesting.name: Excessive nesting depth (JavaScript, 6+ levels)
js_deep_nesting.risk: Code nested more than 5 levels deep is extremely difficult to read, test, and maintain. Deep nesting in JavaScript often results from callback patterns.
js_deep_nesting.solution: Apply early return / guard clauses. Use async/await instead of nested callbacks to reduce callback hell.
js_deep_nesting.benefit: Linear code is easier to understand, test, and modify — especially for asynchronous JavaScript.

js_cognitive_complexity.name: High cognitive complexity (JavaScript)
js_cognitive_complexity.risk: A function with many conditional branches, loops, and logical operators is hard to understand, test, and reason about all possible execution paths.
js_cognitive_complexity.solution: Break the function into smaller, focused functions with a single responsibility. Extract complex conditions into well-named boolean variables.
js_cognitive_complexity.benefit: Small, focused functions are easier to read, test individually, and reuse.

local_time_usage.name: Local Time Without Timezone
local_time_usage.risk: Using datetime.now() or new Date() without timezone produces inconsistent timestamps across servers in different timezones (CWE-187).
local_time_usage.solution: Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) in Python, new Date().toISOString() in JavaScript, or explicit UTC-based time functions.
local_time_usage.benefit: Consistent timestamps across distributed systems, correct log correlation and event ordering.

hardcoded_internal_ip.name: Hardcoded Internal IP Address
hardcoded_internal_ip.risk: Private IP addresses (10.x, 192.168.x, 172.16-31.x) hardcoded in source code expose internal network topology and break across environments (CWE-798).
hardcoded_internal_ip.solution: Use environment variables, configuration files, or service discovery for internal addresses.
hardcoded_internal_ip.benefit: Network topology hidden from source code, portable across environments, easier infrastructure changes.

missing_csp_header.name: Missing Content-Security-Policy
missing_csp_header.risk: Web application without Content-Security-Policy header is vulnerable to XSS, clickjacking, and data injection attacks (CWE-1021).
missing_csp_header.solution: Add CSP headers via flask-talisman (Flask), django-csp (Django), or helmet (Express). Start with a restrictive policy.
missing_csp_header.benefit: Defense-in-depth against XSS, reduced impact of injection vulnerabilities, browser-enforced security policy.

exposed_test_endpoint.name: Exposed Test/Debug Endpoint
exposed_test_endpoint.risk: Test or debug endpoints (/test, /debug, /_debug) without authentication can expose internal state, bypass security controls, or enable data exfiltration (CWE-489).
exposed_test_endpoint.solution: Remove test endpoints from production code, or protect them with authentication and restrict to internal networks.
exposed_test_endpoint.benefit: Reduced attack surface, no accidental exposure of internal application state or debug information.

missing_health_check.name: Missing Health Check Endpoint
missing_health_check.risk: Application with API routes but no health check endpoint (/health, /readiness, /ping) — load balancers and orchestrators cannot verify service availability, reducing redundancy effectiveness (ISO A.8.14).
missing_health_check.solution: Add a /health or /readiness endpoint that returns service status. Integrate with load balancer health checks and container orchestration probes.
missing_health_check.benefit: Enables automated failover, load balancer health monitoring, and container orchestration liveness/readiness probes.

unreviewed_vendor_code.name: Unreviewed Vendor Code
unreviewed_vendor_code.risk: Vendor or third-party code directory without LICENSE, NOTICE, or security review documentation — outsourced code may contain vulnerabilities, backdoors, or license violations without governance controls (ISO A.8.30).
unreviewed_vendor_code.solution: Add LICENSE and SECURITY_REVIEW files to vendor directories. Conduct security review of all third-party code before integration. Document vendor agreements and review dates.
unreviewed_vendor_code.benefit: Controlled supply chain, documented vendor code provenance, reduced risk of undiscovered vulnerabilities in outsourced components.

jndi_injection_java.name: JNDI Injection (Log4Shell)
jndi_injection_java.risk: Allows remote code execution via JNDI lookup with user-controlled input (CVE-2021-44228).
jndi_injection_java.solution: Never pass user input to JNDI lookups. Update Log4j to 2.17+. Disable JNDI lookup via -Dlog4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true.
jndi_injection_java.benefit: Prevents critical remote code execution attacks.

xpath_injection_java.name: XPath Injection (Java)
xpath_injection_java.risk: User input concatenated into XPath expressions allows query manipulation, data extraction, or authentication bypass (CWE-643).
xpath_injection_java.solution: Use parameterized XPath queries (XPathExpression with variables) or sanitize input with a strict allowlist.
xpath_injection_java.benefit: Prevents unauthorized data access and authentication bypass via XPath manipulation.

xpath_injection_csharp.name: XPath Injection (C#)
xpath_injection_csharp.risk: User input concatenated into XPath expressions allows query manipulation, data extraction, or authentication bypass (CWE-643).
xpath_injection_csharp.solution: Use XPathExpression.Compile with XsltArgumentList for variables, or validate input against a strict allowlist.
xpath_injection_csharp.benefit: Prevents unauthorized data access and authentication bypass via XPath manipulation.

xpath_injection_php.name: XPath Injection (PHP)
xpath_injection_php.risk: User input concatenated into XPath queries via DOMXPath::query allows data extraction or authentication bypass (CWE-643).
xpath_injection_php.solution: Use parameterized XPath queries or sanitize input with a strict allowlist. Avoid string concatenation in XPath expressions.
xpath_injection_php.benefit: Prevents unauthorized data access and authentication bypass via XPath manipulation.

xpath_injection_python.name: XPath Injection (Python)
xpath_injection_python.risk: User input concatenated into lxml or ElementTree XPath expressions allows query manipulation or data extraction (CWE-643).
xpath_injection_python.solution: Use lxml XPath variables (xpath expr, var=value) or sanitize input with a strict allowlist.
xpath_injection_python.benefit: Prevents unauthorized data access via XPath manipulation.

ssti_python.name: Server-Side Template Injection (Python)
ssti_python.risk: User input passed directly to template rendering (Jinja2, Mako, Django) allows arbitrary code execution on the server (CWE-1336).
ssti_python.solution: Never render user input as a template string. Use template files with context variables. Enable Jinja2 sandboxed environment.
ssti_python.benefit: Prevents remote code execution via template engine exploitation.

ssti_javascript.name: Server-Side Template Injection (JavaScript)
ssti_javascript.risk: User input passed directly to template engines (Pug, EJS, Handlebars) allows arbitrary code execution on the server (CWE-1336).
ssti_javascript.solution: Never render user input as a template string. Use precompiled templates with context variables. Avoid eval-based template engines.
ssti_javascript.benefit: Prevents remote code execution via template engine exploitation.

csv_injection.name: CSV Formula Injection
csv_injection.risk: User input starting with =, +, -, or @ written to CSV files can execute formulas when opened in spreadsheet software (CWE-1236).
csv_injection.solution: Prefix cell values starting with formula characters with a single quote or tab. Sanitize user input before CSV export.
csv_injection.benefit: Prevents code execution when CSV files are opened in spreadsheet applications.

smtp_injection_python.name: SMTP Header Injection (Python)
smtp_injection_python.risk: User input injected into email headers (To, CC, Subject) can add arbitrary recipients or modify email content via newline characters (CWE-93).
smtp_injection_python.solution: Validate and sanitize email addresses. Reject input containing newline characters (\r, \n). Use email libraries that handle header encoding.
smtp_injection_python.benefit: Prevents email spam relay and phishing attacks via header manipulation.

smtp_injection_php.name: SMTP Header Injection (PHP)
smtp_injection_php.risk: User input injected into mail() headers can add arbitrary recipients or modify email content via newline characters (CWE-93).
smtp_injection_php.solution: Validate and sanitize email addresses. Reject input containing newline characters. Use PHPMailer or Symfony Mailer instead of mail().
smtp_injection_php.benefit: Prevents email spam relay and phishing attacks via header manipulation.

redos_vulnerable.name: ReDoS Vulnerable Regex
redos_vulnerable.risk: Regular expression with nested quantifiers or overlapping alternations causes catastrophic backtracking, leading to CPU exhaustion (CWE-1333).
redos_vulnerable.solution: Simplify regex patterns to avoid nested quantifiers. Use atomic groups or possessive quantifiers. Set timeout for regex evaluation.
redos_vulnerable.benefit: Prevents denial of service via CPU exhaustion from malicious input.

format_string_vuln.name: Format String Vulnerability
format_string_vuln.risk: User input used as format string in logging or string formatting functions allows information disclosure or crashes (CWE-134).
format_string_vuln.solution: Always pass user input as arguments to format functions, never as the format string itself. Use logger.info('msg: %s', user_input) instead of logger.info(user_input).
format_string_vuln.benefit: Prevents information disclosure and application crashes via format string attacks.

missing_hsts.name: Missing HSTS Header
missing_hsts.risk: Web application without Strict-Transport-Security header allows downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking on first visit (CWE-319).
missing_hsts.solution: Add Strict-Transport-Security header with max-age of at least 31536000 (1 year). Include includeSubDomains and preload directives.
missing_hsts.benefit: Forces HTTPS connections, prevents SSL stripping and downgrade attacks.

missing_x_content_type_options.name: Missing X-Content-Type-Options
missing_x_content_type_options.risk: Without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, browsers may MIME-sniff responses, enabling XSS via content type confusion (CWE-16).
missing_x_content_type_options.solution: Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header to all responses. Configure at web server or framework level.
missing_x_content_type_options.benefit: Prevents MIME-type confusion attacks and reduces XSS attack surface.

missing_referrer_policy.name: Missing Referrer-Policy
missing_referrer_policy.risk: Without Referrer-Policy header, sensitive data in URLs (tokens, session IDs) may leak to third-party sites via the Referer header (CWE-200).
missing_referrer_policy.solution: Add Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin or no-referrer header. Configure at web server or framework level.
missing_referrer_policy.benefit: Prevents leakage of sensitive URL data to external sites.

missing_frame_protection.name: Missing X-Frame-Options
missing_frame_protection.risk: Without X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, the page can be embedded in iframes enabling clickjacking attacks (CWE-1021).
missing_frame_protection.solution: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN header, or use CSP frame-ancestors directive.
missing_frame_protection.benefit: Prevents clickjacking attacks by blocking unauthorized framing of the page.

postmessage_no_origin_check.name: postMessage Without Origin Check
postmessage_no_origin_check.risk: Event listener for postMessage without origin validation accepts messages from any source, enabling cross-origin data injection (CWE-346).
postmessage_no_origin_check.solution: Always check event.origin against a trusted allowlist before processing postMessage data.
postmessage_no_origin_check.benefit: Prevents cross-origin attacks via malicious postMessage from untrusted windows.

missing_sri.name: Missing Subresource Integrity
missing_sri.risk: External scripts or stylesheets loaded without integrity attribute can be tampered with if the CDN is compromised (CWE-353).
missing_sri.solution: Add integrity attribute with SHA-256/384/512 hash and crossorigin='anonymous' to external script and link tags.
missing_sri.benefit: Ensures external resources have not been tampered with, protects against CDN compromise.

svg_scriptable_content.name: SVG With Scriptable Content
svg_scriptable_content.risk: SVG files containing <script> tags, event handlers (onload, onclick), or foreignObject elements can execute JavaScript when rendered (CWE-79).
svg_scriptable_content.solution: Sanitize SVG files to remove script elements, event handlers, and foreignObject. Use a SVG sanitizer library or Content-Security-Policy.
svg_scriptable_content.benefit: Prevents XSS attacks via malicious SVG content.

graphql_introspection_enabled.name: GraphQL Introspection Enabled
graphql_introspection_enabled.risk: GraphQL introspection enabled in production exposes the full API schema, including sensitive fields and internal types (CWE-200).
graphql_introspection_enabled.solution: Disable introspection in production. Use middleware or server configuration to block __schema and __type queries.
graphql_introspection_enabled.benefit: Prevents API schema disclosure and reduces attack surface for targeted exploitation.

graphql_no_depth_limit.name: GraphQL Without Depth Limit
graphql_no_depth_limit.risk: GraphQL endpoint without query depth limiting allows deeply nested queries that cause excessive resource consumption (CWE-400).
graphql_no_depth_limit.solution: Implement query depth limiting (max 10-15 levels). Use graphql-depth-limit (JS) or similar middleware. Add query complexity analysis.
graphql_no_depth_limit.benefit: Prevents denial of service via deeply nested GraphQL queries.

websocket_no_tls.name: WebSocket Without TLS
websocket_no_tls.risk: WebSocket connection using ws:// instead of wss:// transmits data in plaintext, vulnerable to eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks (CWE-319).
websocket_no_tls.solution: Always use wss:// for WebSocket connections. Configure TLS at the server level.
websocket_no_tls.benefit: Ensures WebSocket communication is encrypted, preventing eavesdropping and tampering.

file_upload_no_validation.name: File Upload Without Validation
file_upload_no_validation.risk: File upload endpoint without validation of file type, size, or content allows uploading of malicious files (web shells, malware) (CWE-434).
file_upload_no_validation.solution: Validate file type via content inspection (magic bytes), not just extension. Enforce size limits. Store files outside web root with randomized names.
file_upload_no_validation.benefit: Prevents remote code execution and malware distribution via file upload.

weak_password_policy.name: Weak Password Policy
weak_password_policy.risk: Password validation accepting short or simple passwords without complexity requirements weakens authentication security (CWE-521).
weak_password_policy.solution: Enforce minimum length of 12 characters. Require mix of character types. Check against common password lists. Implement account lockout.
weak_password_policy.benefit: Strengthens authentication against brute-force and credential stuffing attacks.

default_credentials.name: Default Credentials
default_credentials.risk: Hardcoded default usernames and passwords (admin/admin, root/root, test/test) remain in production, providing easy unauthorized access (CWE-1392).
default_credentials.solution: Remove all default credentials. Force password change on first login. Use environment variables for initial admin setup.
default_credentials.benefit: Eliminates trivial unauthorized access via well-known default credentials.

security_questions.name: Security Questions Usage
security_questions.risk: Security questions for authentication recovery are easily guessable or discoverable via social engineering, weakening account security (CWE-640).
security_questions.solution: Replace security questions with multi-factor authentication (TOTP, WebAuthn). Use secure password reset via email with time-limited tokens.
security_questions.benefit: Stronger account recovery mechanism resistant to social engineering attacks.

jwt_none_algorithm.name: JWT None Algorithm
jwt_none_algorithm.risk: JWT verification accepting 'none' algorithm allows forging tokens without a valid signature, bypassing authentication entirely (CWE-327).
jwt_none_algorithm.solution: Explicitly specify allowed algorithms in JWT verification. Never accept 'none'. Use algorithms=['HS256'] or algorithms=['RS256'].
jwt_none_algorithm.benefit: Prevents authentication bypass via unsigned JWT tokens.

jwt_hardcoded_secret.name: JWT Hardcoded Secret
jwt_hardcoded_secret.risk: JWT signing secret hardcoded in source code allows anyone with code access to forge valid tokens (CWE-798).
jwt_hardcoded_secret.solution: Store JWT secrets in environment variables or a secrets manager. Rotate secrets regularly. Use asymmetric keys (RS256) for distributed systems.
jwt_hardcoded_secret.benefit: Prevents token forgery by keeping signing keys out of source code.

insufficient_key_size.name: Insufficient Cryptographic Key Size
insufficient_key_size.risk: Cryptographic keys below recommended sizes (RSA < 2048, AES < 128, EC < 256 bits) are vulnerable to brute-force attacks (CWE-326).
insufficient_key_size.solution: Use RSA 2048+ bits, AES 128+ bits, EC 256+ bits. Follow NIST SP 800-57 guidelines for key size selection.
insufficient_key_size.benefit: Ensures cryptographic operations resist brute-force attacks with current and near-future computing power.

log_injection.name: Log Injection
log_injection.risk: User input written directly to log entries without sanitization allows log forging, log poisoning, or CRLF injection into log files (CWE-117).
log_injection.solution: Sanitize user input before logging by removing or escaping newline characters (\r, \n). Use structured logging (JSON format) to prevent injection.
log_injection.benefit: Preserves log integrity, prevents log analysis evasion and downstream log processing exploits.

ssl_no_cert_validation.name: SSL cert validation disabled
ssl_no_cert_validation.risk: verify=False disables SSL certificate validation, exposing connections to man-in-the-middle attacks (CWE-295).
ssl_no_cert_validation.solution: Remove verify=False or configure a trusted certificate bundle.
ssl_no_cert_validation.benefit: Verified HTTPS connections, protection against interception.

os_system_injection.name: Shell execution via os.system/popen
os_system_injection.risk: os.system() and os.popen() execute shell commands, vulnerable to command injection (CWE-78).
os_system_injection.solution: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and an argument list.

insecure_cipher.name: Insecure cipher algorithm
insecure_cipher.risk: DES, ARC4, Blowfish and other obsolete algorithms are cryptographically weak (CWE-327).
insecure_cipher.benefit: Robust encryption conforming to current standards.

ecb_cipher_mode.name: Insecure ECB cipher mode
ecb_cipher_mode.risk: ECB mode produces identical blocks for identical data, exposing patterns (CWE-327).
ecb_cipher_mode.solution: Use GCM or CBC mode with a random IV.

insecure_ssl_version.name: Insecure SSL/TLS version
insecure_ssl_version.risk: SSLv2, SSLv3 and TLSv1.0/1.1 have known vulnerabilities (POODLE, BEAST, CRIME) (CWE-327).
insecure_ssl_version.benefit: Protection against attacks on obsolete protocols.

permissive_file_permissions.name: Permissive file permissions
permissive_file_permissions.risk: os.chmod with 0o777/0o766 makes files accessible to all users (CWE-732).
permissive_file_permissions.solution: Use restrictive permissions (0o600 for secrets, 0o644 for public files).

hardcoded_tmp_path.name: Hardcoded /tmp path
hardcoded_tmp_path.risk: Hardcoded /tmp paths are vulnerable to symlink attacks and race conditions (CWE-377).
hardcoded_tmp_path.solution: Use tempfile.mkdtemp() or tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() for secure temporary paths.
hardcoded_tmp_path.benefit: Unique temporary paths protected against race conditions.

django_mark_safe_xss.name: Django mark_safe() — XSS risk
django_mark_safe_xss.risk: mark_safe() disables HTML escaping, exposing to script injection if content includes user data (CWE-79).
django_mark_safe_xss.solution: Use Django auto-escaping or format_html() for safe HTML.

tarfile_unsafe_extract.name: Unsafe tar extraction
tarfile_unsafe_extract.risk: tarfile.extractall() without filtering allows writing files outside the target directory via relative paths (CWE-22).
tarfile_unsafe_extract.solution: Use extractall(filter='data') (Python 3.12+) or validate each member before extraction.
tarfile_unsafe_extract.benefit: Protection against path traversal via tar archives.

paramiko_no_host_key.name: Paramiko no host key verification
paramiko_no_host_key.risk: AutoAddPolicy automatically accepts any SSH key, vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks (CWE-295).
paramiko_no_host_key.solution: Use RejectPolicy or a verified known_hosts file.
paramiko_no_host_key.benefit: Authenticated SSH connections, protection against server spoofing.

prototype_pollution.name: Prototype pollution
prototype_pollution.risk: Object.assign or __proto__ with user data allows modifying the global prototype and injecting properties (CWE-1321).
prototype_pollution.solution: Use Object.create(null) or Map, validate keys with a whitelist.
prototype_pollution.benefit: Protection against property injection on all objects.

regex_dos.name: ReDoS — unsafe regex
regex_dos.risk: A regex built from user data can cause denial of service via exponential backtracking (CWE-1333).
regex_dos.solution: Never build regex from user data. Use safe-regex or re2.
regex_dos.benefit: Protection against regex-based denial of service.

open_redirect.name: Open redirect
open_redirect.risk: res.redirect() with user-controlled URL allows redirection to malicious sites (CWE-601).
open_redirect.solution: Validate redirect URL against an allowlist of authorized paths.

jwt_weak_secret.name: JWT weak secret
jwt_weak_secret.risk: A JWT secret shorter than 16 characters is vulnerable to brute force (CWE-326).
jwt_weak_secret.solution: Use a secret of at least 32 random characters or an RSA/EC key.

express_no_csrf.name: Express without CSRF protection
express_no_csrf.risk: POST/PUT/DELETE routes without CSRF middleware are vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CWE-352).
express_no_csrf.solution: Add csurf or lusca as CSRF middleware.

mongo_operator_injection.name: MongoDB NoSQL injection
mongo_operator_injection.risk: User data passed directly to find/update allows operator injection ($gt, $ne) to bypass filters (CWE-943).
mongo_operator_injection.solution: Use express-mongo-sanitize or validate parameter types.

eval_template_literal.name: eval() with template literal
eval_template_literal.risk: eval() with a template literal allows arbitrary code execution (CWE-94).
eval_template_literal.solution: Never use eval(). Use safe alternatives (JSON.parse, isolated Function constructor).

unsafe_require.name: require() with dynamic variable
unsafe_require.risk: require() with a non-literal path allows loading arbitrary modules (CWE-94).
unsafe_require.solution: Use only literal paths in require(). Validate inputs if dynamic loading is needed.

vue_v_html.name: Vue.js v-html — XSS risk
vue_v_html.risk: v-html directive injects raw HTML without escaping, vulnerable to XSS if content includes user data (CWE-79).
vue_v_html.solution: Use {{ }} interpolation or v-text. Sanitize with DOMPurify if v-html is needed.

svelte_at_html.name: Svelte {@html} — XSS risk
svelte_at_html.risk: {@html} injects raw HTML without escaping in Svelte (CWE-79).
svelte_at_html.solution: Use text interpolation {variable} or sanitize with DOMPurify.

cors_credentials_wildcard.name: CORS wildcard with credentials
cors_credentials_wildcard.risk: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with credentials: true is rejected by browsers but indicates misconfiguration (CWE-942).
cors_credentials_wildcard.solution: Explicitly specify allowed origins instead of wildcard.

window_open_noopener.name: window.open without noopener
window_open_noopener.risk: window.open() without rel='noopener' allows the opened page to access window.opener (CWE-1022).

npm_lifecycle_script.name: Suspicious npm lifecycle script
npm_lifecycle_script.risk: preinstall/postinstall scripts in package.json can execute arbitrary code during npm install (CWE-506).
npm_lifecycle_script.solution: Verify lifecycle scripts are legitimate (husky, prisma generate). Remove unknown scripts.
npm_lifecycle_script.benefit: Protection against npm supply chain attacks.

base64_eval.name: Base64 obfuscated code execution
base64_eval.risk: eval/exec on base64-decoded content hides malicious code to bypass security tools (CWE-506).
base64_eval.solution: Never execute base64-decoded code. Use JSON.parse for structured data.

base64_obfuscation.name: Suspicious base64 string decoded
base64_obfuscation.risk: A long base64 string decoded by atob() may contain obfuscated malicious code (CWE-506).
base64_obfuscation.solution: Verify decoded content. Prefer readable formats (JSON, plain text).

javascript_uri.name: javascript: URI — XSS
javascript_uri.risk: javascript: URIs execute code in page context, enabling cookie theft and redirection (CWE-79).
javascript_uri.solution: Use event handlers (addEventListener) instead of javascript: URIs.

javascript_uri_html.name: javascript: URI in HTML attribute
javascript_uri_html.risk: href/action/src with javascript: executes arbitrary code on click or load (CWE-79).
javascript_uri_html.solution: Use normal URIs (/, #, https://) and event handlers.

data_uri_html.name: Data URI with HTML content
data_uri_html.risk: data:text/html allows injecting executable HTML/JS in an iframe or image (CWE-79).
data_uri_html.solution: Forbid data: URIs with text/html. Validate and sanitize sources.
data_uri_html.benefit: Protection against HTML injection via data URIs.

data_uri_html_tag.name: Data URI HTML in tag
data_uri_html_tag.risk: src/href with data:text/html loads executable HTML content directly in the browser (CWE-79).
data_uri_html_tag.solution: Forbid data:text/html in src and href attributes.

inline_event_handler.name: Inline event handler
inline_event_handler.risk: on* attributes (onerror, onload, onclick) execute JavaScript without script tags, bypassing some CSP protections (CWE-79).
inline_event_handler.solution: Use addEventListener() instead of inline on* attributes.

inline_event_handler_html.name: Inline event handler in HTML
inline_event_handler_html.risk: on* attributes in HTML execute JavaScript directly, vulnerable to XSS (CWE-79).
inline_event_handler_html.solution: Move JavaScript to separate .js files with addEventListener().

base64_credentials.name: Base64 encoded credentials
base64_credentials.risk: Base64 is NOT encryption — credentials are readable by simple decoding (CWE-312).
base64_credentials.solution: Use environment variables or a secrets manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager).
base64_credentials.benefit: Secrets not exposed in source code.

crud_without_ownership.name: CRUD without ownership check
crud_without_ownership.risk: Users can access or modify resources belonging to other users (IDOR).
crud_without_ownership.solution: Verify resource ownership before every CRUD operation.
crud_without_ownership.benefit: Prevents unauthorized access to other users' data.

heading_skip_level.name: Heading skip level
heading_skip_level.risk: Screen readers misinterpret the page structure when heading levels are skipped.
heading_skip_level.solution: Use sequential heading levels (h1 → h2 → h3, never skip).
heading_skip_level.benefit: Correct page structure for assistive technologies.

html_no_lang.name: HTML missing lang attribute
html_no_lang.risk: Screen readers cannot determine the page language, affecting pronunciation.
html_no_lang.solution: Add lang attribute to the html element: <html lang="en">.
html_no_lang.benefit: Correct pronunciation for screen reader users.

http_smuggling.name: HTTP request smuggling
http_smuggling.risk: Inconsistent Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding headers enable request smuggling attacks.
http_smuggling.solution: Normalize headers server-side and reject ambiguous requests.
http_smuggling.benefit: Prevents request smuggling and cache poisoning attacks.

iframe_no_title.name: Iframe without title
iframe_no_title.risk: Screen readers cannot describe the iframe purpose to users.
iframe_no_title.solution: Add a descriptive title attribute to every iframe.
iframe_no_title.benefit: Iframes are identifiable by assistive technologies.

img_decorative_no_role.name: Decorative image without role
img_decorative_no_role.risk: Screen readers announce decorative images, creating noise for users.
img_decorative_no_role.solution: Add role="presentation" or aria-hidden="true" to decorative images.
img_decorative_no_role.benefit: Decorative images are properly hidden from screen readers.

insecure_deserialize_call.name: Insecure deserialization call
insecure_deserialize_call.risk: Deserializing untrusted data can lead to remote code execution.
insecure_deserialize_call.solution: Use safe alternatives: json.loads(), yaml.safe_load() instead of pickle/marshal.

link_no_text.name: Link without text
link_no_text.risk: Screen readers cannot describe the link destination to users.
link_no_text.solution: Add visible text or aria-label to every link.
link_no_text.benefit: All links are accessible and understandable.

html_invalid_aria_role.name: Empty ARIA role attribute
html_invalid_aria_role.risk: An empty role attribute is invalid and confuses assistive technologies that rely on it to determine element semantics.
html_invalid_aria_role.solution: Remove the empty role attribute or set a valid ARIA role (e.g. button, dialog, navigation, main).
html_invalid_aria_role.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 4.1.2 — Name, Role, Value — ensures correct semantics for assistive technologies.

html_aria_hidden_focusable.name: Focusable element hidden with aria-hidden
html_aria_hidden_focusable.risk: A focusable element hidden from assistive technologies with aria-hidden="true" can still receive keyboard focus, creating a confusing experience for screen reader users.
html_aria_hidden_focusable.solution: Do not use aria-hidden="true" on focusable elements. Use tabindex="-1" to remove the element from the keyboard flow, or restructure the DOM.
html_aria_hidden_focusable.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 — keyboard navigation remains coherent and predictable for all users.

html_viewport_zoom_disabled.name: User zoom disabled (viewport)
html_viewport_zoom_disabled.risk: Disabling pinch-to-zoom with user-scalable=no prevents users with low vision from enlarging content, making the page effectively unusable for them.
html_viewport_zoom_disabled.solution: Remove user-scalable=no from the viewport meta tag. Allow users to zoom freely.
html_viewport_zoom_disabled.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.4.4 — Resize Text — users can scale content up to 200% without loss of functionality.

html_select_missing_label.name: Select without accessible label
html_select_missing_label.risk: A select element without a label or aria-label provides no accessible name, making it impossible for screen reader users to understand what data to choose.
html_select_missing_label.solution: Associate a <label for="id"> element with the select, or add an aria-label attribute directly on the select.
html_select_missing_label.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 and 4.1.2 — all form controls have an accessible name understandable by assistive technologies.

html_input_button_empty.name: Button input without label (missing value)
html_input_button_empty.risk: A submit, reset, or button input without a value attribute has no accessible label. Screen readers announce it as "button" with no description.
html_input_button_empty.solution: Add a value attribute with a descriptive label, or replace with a <button> element with visible text content.
html_input_button_empty.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 4.1.2 — Name, Role, Value — every interactive control has an accessible name.

html_autocomplete_invalid.name: Non-standard autocomplete value
html_autocomplete_invalid.risk: Using non-standard values like "yes", "true", or "false" for the autocomplete attribute is invalid HTML5. Browsers and assistive technologies may ignore or misinterpret the attribute.
html_autocomplete_invalid.solution: Use standard autocomplete values defined in the HTML5 spec: "on", "off", "email", "username", "current-password", "new-password", "name", "tel", etc.
html_autocomplete_invalid.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.5 — Identify Input Purpose — allows browsers and assistive tools to correctly autofill form fields.

html_th_scope_missing.name: Table header without scope attribute
html_th_scope_missing.risk: A table header cell without a scope attribute leaves screen readers unable to determine which data cells it applies to, making complex tables inaccessible.
html_th_scope_missing.solution: Add scope="col" for column headers or scope="row" for row headers on every <th> element.
html_th_scope_missing.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.1 — Info and Relationships — table structure is programmatically determinable by assistive technologies.

html_missing_main_landmark.name: Missing <main> landmark
html_missing_main_landmark.risk: A page without a main landmark (<main> or role="main") forces screen reader users to navigate through all content without a shortcut to the primary content, significantly increasing cognitive load.
html_missing_main_landmark.solution: Wrap the primary page content in a <main> element. Only one <main> per page.
html_missing_main_landmark.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.3.6 and 2.4.1 — Bypass Blocks — users can jump directly to the main content.

html_invalid_lang_value.name: Non-BCP-47 lang attribute value
html_invalid_lang_value.risk: Using language names in plain text (e.g. lang="french") instead of BCP 47 codes (e.g. lang="fr") is invalid. Screen readers and translation tools rely on valid language codes.
html_invalid_lang_value.solution: Use valid BCP 47 language codes: lang="fr" (French), lang="en" (English), lang="es" (Spanish), lang="de" (German), lang="it" (Italian), lang="pt" (Portuguese), etc.
html_invalid_lang_value.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 — Language of Page/Parts — correct language identification enables proper pronunciation by screen readers.

html_video_missing_captions.name: Video without caption track
html_video_missing_captions.risk: A video element without a caption track (<track kind="captions">) makes the content inaccessible to deaf and hard-of-hearing users who cannot perceive the audio information.
html_video_missing_captions.solution: Add a <track kind="captions"> element inside the <video> tag pointing to a WebVTT (.vtt) or SRT subtitle file.
html_video_missing_captions.benefit: Compliance with WCAG 1.2.2 — Captions (Prerecorded) — all synchronized media has captions for deaf and hard-of-hearing users.

html_inline_style.name: Inline CSS style (HTML)
html_inline_style.risk: Inline styles tightly couple HTML structure with presentation. They cannot be overridden by external stylesheets without !important and are difficult to maintain at scale.
html_inline_style.solution: Move styles to an external CSS file or CSS module. Use CSS classes for reusable styles.
html_inline_style.benefit: Clean separation of concerns — HTML defines structure, CSS defines presentation. Styles are maintainable and reusable.

html_deprecated_tag.name: Deprecated HTML tag
html_deprecated_tag.risk: Deprecated HTML elements (font, center, marquee, blink, etc.) were removed from HTML5. Their behavior is unpredictable across browsers and assistive technologies.
html_deprecated_tag.solution: Replace with modern HTML5 equivalents and CSS for all visual presentation.
html_deprecated_tag.benefit: Standard-compliant HTML rendering consistently across all modern browsers and assistive technologies.

html_button_missing_type.name: HTML button without type attribute
html_button_missing_type.risk: A <button> without a type attribute defaults to type="submit". Inside a form, this causes accidental form submissions when the button is clicked for another purpose.
html_button_missing_type.solution: Always specify the type attribute: type="button" for actions, type="submit" for form submission, type="reset" for form reset.
html_button_missing_type.benefit: Explicit, predictable button behavior — no accidental form submissions.

html_img_missing_dimensions.name: HTML image without dimensions (width/height)
html_img_missing_dimensions.risk: An without explicit width and height attributes causes Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) — the browser does not reserve space while the image loads, causing content to jump.
html_img_missing_dimensions.solution: Add explicit width and height attributes matching the image's intrinsic dimensions.
html_img_missing_dimensions.benefit: Eliminates CLS — the page layout is stable while images load, improving user experience and Core Web Vitals score.

html_target_blank_noreferrer.name: target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer"
html_target_blank_noreferrer.risk: Links with target="_blank" without rel="noopener noreferrer" allow the new page to access window.opener, creating a reverse tabnapping vulnerability and a referrer leak.
html_target_blank_noreferrer.solution: Always add rel="noopener noreferrer" to every link with target="_blank".
html_target_blank_noreferrer.benefit: Prevents reverse tabnapping attacks and referrer leaks — third-party sites opened in new tabs cannot manipulate the original page.

html_missing_meta_viewport.name: Missing viewport meta tag (HTML)
html_missing_meta_viewport.risk: Without a viewport meta tag, mobile browsers render the page at desktop width and scale it down, making text and UI elements unreadably small on mobile devices.
html_missing_meta_viewport.solution: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> in the <head>. Do not add user-scalable=no (see WCAG 1.4.4).
html_missing_meta_viewport.benefit: Responsive design foundation — the page adapts to the device screen width, providing a usable experience on all screen sizes.

missing_doctype.name: Missing DOCTYPE declaration
missing_doctype.risk: Browser renders in quirks mode, causing inconsistent layout and behavior.
missing_doctype.solution: Add <!DOCTYPE html> as the first line of the HTML document.

missing_rate_limit.name: Missing rate limiting
missing_rate_limit.risk: Endpoints without rate limiting are vulnerable to brute force and DoS attacks.
missing_rate_limit.benefit: Protection against brute force and denial of service.

missing_skip_link.name: Missing skip navigation link
missing_skip_link.risk: Keyboard users must tab through all navigation links to reach main content.
missing_skip_link.solution: Add a skip link as the first focusable element: Skip to content.
missing_skip_link.benefit: Keyboard users can quickly access main content.

missing_timeout.name: Missing request timeout
missing_timeout.risk: HTTP requests without timeout can hang indefinitely, causing resource exhaustion.
missing_timeout.solution: Add timeout parameter to all HTTP requests: requests.get(url, timeout=30).
missing_timeout.benefit: Prevents resource exhaustion from hanging connections.

page_no_title.name: Page without title
page_no_title.risk: Users cannot identify the page in browser tabs, bookmarks, or search results.
page_no_title.solution: Add a descriptive <title> element in the <head> section.
page_no_title.benefit: Pages are identifiable in tabs, bookmarks, and search engines.

parser_without_try.name: Parser without error handling
parser_without_try.risk: Unhandled parsing exceptions crash the application and may leak internal details.
parser_without_try.solution: Wrap parsing calls in try/except with appropriate error handling.
parser_without_try.benefit: Graceful error handling prevents crashes and information leakage.

path_traversal_os_join.name: Path traversal via os.path.join
path_traversal_os_join.risk: os.path.join with user input allows directory traversal (../) to access arbitrary files.
path_traversal_os_join.solution: Validate and sanitize paths: use os.path.realpath() and verify the result is within the allowed directory.

redos_nested_quantifier.name: ReDoS nested quantifier
redos_nested_quantifier.risk: Nested regex quantifiers cause catastrophic backtracking, enabling denial of service.
redos_nested_quantifier.solution: Rewrite the regex to avoid nested quantifiers, or use re2/regex with timeout.
redos_nested_quantifier.benefit: Prevents regex-based denial of service attacks.

trust_boundary_python.name: Trust boundary violation
trust_boundary_python.risk: Mixing trusted and untrusted data in the same structure enables injection attacks.
trust_boundary_python.solution: Clearly separate trusted from untrusted data; validate at trust boundaries.
trust_boundary_python.benefit: Clear separation prevents cross-contamination of trusted data.

weak_random_python.name: Weak random number generator
weak_random_python.risk: random module is not cryptographically secure; predictable values enable attacks.
weak_random_python.solution: Use secrets module for security-sensitive operations: secrets.token_hex().
weak_random_python.benefit: Cryptographically secure random values for tokens and keys.

xss_flask_reflected.name: Reflected XSS (Flask)
xss_flask_reflected.risk: User input reflected in HTML without escaping allows script injection.
xss_flask_reflected.solution: Use Jinja2 auto-escaping ({{ variable }}) or markupsafe.escape().

xxe_injection_python.name: XXE injection (Python)
xxe_injection_python.risk: XML parsers with external entity processing enabled allow file disclosure and SSRF.
xxe_injection_python.solution: Use defusedxml library or disable external entity processing.
xxe_injection_python.benefit: Prevents XML-based file disclosure and server-side request forgery.

zip_bomb.name: Zip bomb vulnerability
zip_bomb.risk: Extracting untrusted archives without size limits can exhaust disk space and memory.
zip_bomb.solution: Check uncompressed size before extraction; set extraction limits.
zip_bomb.benefit: Prevents denial of service from malicious archives.

unrestricted_file_upload_java.name: Unrestricted file upload (Java/Spring)
unrestricted_file_upload_java.risk: MultipartFile.transferTo() or getOriginalFilename() without file type validation allows uploading of web shells and malicious executables (CWE-434, OWASP A04).
unrestricted_file_upload_java.solution: Validate file type via magic bytes (Apache Tika), enforce a strict allowlist of extensions, and store files outside the web root with randomized names.
unrestricted_file_upload_java.benefit: Prevents web shell uploads and arbitrary code execution via unrestricted file upload (CWE-434).

unrestricted_file_upload_php.name: Unrestricted file upload (PHP)
unrestricted_file_upload_php.risk: move_uploaded_file() without file type or extension validation allows uploading of PHP web shells and malicious scripts (CWE-434, OWASP A04).
unrestricted_file_upload_php.solution: Validate file type via finfo_file() magic bytes, check extension against a strict allowlist, and store files outside the web root with randomized names.
unrestricted_file_upload_php.benefit: Prevents PHP web shell uploads and arbitrary code execution (CWE-434).

unrestricted_file_upload_js.name: Unrestricted file upload (Node.js/Multer)
unrestricted_file_upload_js.risk: Multer configured without a fileFilter allows uploading of any file type, including JavaScript files and web shells that could execute server-side (CWE-434, OWASP A04).
unrestricted_file_upload_js.solution: Always configure multer with a fileFilter function that validates MIME type and extension against a strict allowlist.
unrestricted_file_upload_js.benefit: Prevents unrestricted file upload attacks leading to remote code execution (CWE-434).

weak_password_hash_php.name: Weak password hashing (PHP)
weak_password_hash_php.risk: Using MD5, SHA1, or SHA256 to hash passwords provides insufficient computational cost — crackable in seconds with GPU-based dictionary attacks (CWE-916, OWASP A02).
weak_password_hash_php.solution: Use PHP's password_hash($password, PASSWORD_BCRYPT) or PASSWORD_ARGON2ID. Verify with password_verify().
weak_password_hash_php.benefit: Ensures password hashes are computationally expensive to crack, resisting offline brute-force attacks (CWE-916).

csrf_missing_flask.name: Missing CSRF protection (Flask)
csrf_missing_flask.risk: Flask POST/PUT/DELETE routes without CSRF protection allow attackers to forge authenticated requests from any website visited by the victim (CWE-352, OWASP A01).
csrf_missing_flask.solution: Use Flask-WTF (CSRFProtect) for server-rendered forms, or implement SameSite=Strict cookies with token-based authentication for REST APIs.
csrf_missing_flask.benefit: Prevents cross-site request forgery attacks that allow unauthorized state-changing actions (CWE-352).

regex_redos_js.name: ReDoS via user-controlled RegExp (JavaScript)
regex_redos_js.risk: Constructing a RegExp from user-controlled input allows ReDoS — an attacker can craft a malicious string causing catastrophic backtracking, blocking the Node.js event loop (CWE-400, OWASP A06).
regex_redos_js.solution: Never construct RegExp from user input. Use safe string matching or escape special characters before creating a bounded regex.
regex_redos_js.benefit: Prevents denial of service attacks via crafted regex inputs in the Node.js event loop (CWE-400).

api_key_in_url.name: API Key in URL
api_key_in_url.risk: API keys in URLs are logged by web servers, proxies, and browsers (CWE-598).
api_key_in_url.solution: Send API keys in the Authorization header, never in the URL.
api_key_in_url.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

cache_poisoning.name: Cache Poisoning
cache_poisoning.risk: X-Forwarded-Host and similar headers, if used without validation, allow cache poisoning. A single poisoned response serves malicious content to all users (CWE-444).
cache_poisoning.solution: Validate X-Forwarded-Host against ALLOWED_HOSTS. Use Vary headers. Configure CDN to not cache responses with unrecognized headers.
cache_poisoning.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

command_injection_java_broad.name: Command Injection (Java)
command_injection_java_broad.risk: System command executed in a file containing HTTP request parameters — potential command injection (CWE-78).
command_injection_java_broad.solution: Avoid passing user input to system commands. Use parameterized APIs instead of shell execution.
command_injection_java_broad.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

dependency_confusion.name: Dependency Confusion
dependency_confusion.risk: If an internal package name exists on public npm, an attacker can publish a malicious version (CWE-427).
dependency_confusion.solution: Use npm scoped packages (@company/pkg). Configure .npmrc with registry for your scope.
dependency_confusion.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

dom_clobbering.name: DOM Clobbering
dom_clobbering.risk: Elements named location , document , etc. override global JavaScript properties, enabling XSS or logic bypass (CWE-79).
dom_clobbering.solution: Avoid using JavaScript global property names as HTML element id or name attributes.
dom_clobbering.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

fstring_in_logging.name: F-string in Logging
fstring_in_logging.risk: f-strings in logging are evaluated even when the log level is disabled (performance). They also bypass log injection sanitization (CWE-117).
fstring_in_logging.solution: Use logger.info("User %s logged in", username) instead of logger.info(f"User {username} logged in").
fstring_in_logging.benefit: Improves logging performance and keeps log formatting lazy and consistent.

graphql_batching_attack.name: GraphQL Batching Attack
graphql_batching_attack.risk: An attacker can send thousands of operations in a single batched request, causing DoS or brute-forcing authentication (CWE-770).
graphql_batching_attack.solution: Disable batching or limit batch size. Add query cost analysis and rate limiting.
graphql_batching_attack.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

hardcoded_iv_nonce.name: Hardcoded IV/Nonce
hardcoded_iv_nonce.risk: A fixed IV makes encrypted data predictable. Identical plaintexts produce identical ciphertexts, leaking patterns (CWE-329).
hardcoded_iv_nonce.solution: Use os.urandom(16) or secrets.token_bytes(16) to generate a fresh IV per encryption.
hardcoded_iv_nonce.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

idor_missing_ownership.name: IDOR Missing Ownership
idor_missing_ownership.risk: Users can access or modify other users' data by changing the ID parameter. The most common API vulnerability (CWE-639).
idor_missing_ownership.solution: Always filter by current user: Model.objects.filter(pk=id, user=request.user). Use object-level permissions.
idor_missing_ownership.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

insecure_cookie_flag.name: Insecure Cookie Flag
insecure_cookie_flag.risk: Cookie with Secure flag set to false is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections (CWE-614).
insecure_cookie_flag.solution: Set cookie.setSecure(true) to ensure cookies are only sent over HTTPS.
insecure_cookie_flag.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

ldap_injection_java_broad.name: LDAP Injection (Java)
ldap_injection_java_broad.risk: LDAP query executed in a file containing HTTP request parameters — potential LDAP injection (CWE-90).
ldap_injection_java_broad.solution: Use parameterized LDAP queries or escape special characters.
ldap_injection_java_broad.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

llm_output_to_sink.name: LLM Output to Sink
llm_output_to_sink.risk: LLM output is untrusted — if passed to SQL, shell, or file operations, an attacker can use prompt injection to achieve RCE/SQLi (CWE-74).
llm_output_to_sink.solution: Validate and sanitize LLM output before using it in queries, commands, or file operations. Never trust LLM output.
llm_output_to_sink.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

log4shell_jndi.name: Log4Shell (JNDI)
log4shell_jndi.risk: JNDI lookups in log messages enable remote code execution via Log4j (CVE-2021-44228). Even in test/config files this is a red flag.
log4shell_jndi.solution: Update Log4j to 2.17+. Set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true. Remove all JNDI lookup patterns.
log4shell_jndi.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

missing_pkce_oauth.name: Missing PKCE (OAuth)
missing_pkce_oauth.risk: Without PKCE, the OAuth authorization code can be stolen by a malicious app or browser extension (CWE-345).
missing_pkce_oauth.solution: Implement PKCE (RFC 7636). Generate code_verifier and code_challenge for each authorization request.
missing_pkce_oauth.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

missing_session_timeout.name: Missing Session Timeout
missing_session_timeout.risk: Sessions without expiry allow stolen session tokens to be used indefinitely (CWE-613).
missing_session_timeout.solution: Set SESSION_COOKIE_AGE (Django) or permanent_session_lifetime (Flask) to limit session duration.
missing_session_timeout.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

oauth_open_redirect.name: OAuth Open Redirect
oauth_open_redirect.risk: An attacker can steal OAuth tokens by redirecting to a malicious site (CWE-601).
oauth_open_redirect.solution: Validate redirect_uri against a whitelist of allowed URLs registered in the OAuth provider.
oauth_open_redirect.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

path_traversal_fis.name: Path Traversal (FileInputStream)
path_traversal_fis.risk: FileInputStream with user-controlled path allows directory traversal to read arbitrary files (CWE-22).
path_traversal_fis.solution: Validate and canonicalize file paths. Use Path.normalize().startsWith(basePath) to restrict access.
path_traversal_fis.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

pii_in_url.name: PII in URL
pii_in_url.risk: Personal data in URLs is logged by web servers, proxies, CDNs, and browser history. GDPR violation risk (CWE-598).
pii_in_url.solution: Use request body (POST) or path parameters with opaque IDs instead of PII in URLs.
pii_in_url.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

prompt_injection_llm.name: Prompt Injection (LLM)
prompt_injection_llm.risk: An attacker can manipulate the LLM to leak data, bypass instructions, or execute unintended actions.
prompt_injection_llm.solution: Sanitize user input before sending to LLM. Use system prompts with strict boundaries.
prompt_injection_llm.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

race_condition_financial.name: Race Condition (Financial)
race_condition_financial.risk: Concurrent requests can cause double-spending, negative balances, or inventory overselling (CWE-362).
race_condition_financial.solution: Use select_for_update(), F() expressions, or transaction.atomic() with database-level locks.
race_condition_financial.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

razor_html_raw.name: XSS via Html.Raw()
razor_html_raw.risk: Html.Raw() disables Razor automatic HTML encoding. If content includes user data, XSS is possible (CWE-79).
razor_html_raw.solution: Use @Model.Property (auto-encoded) or Html.Encode(). Only use Html.Raw() with trusted, pre-sanitized content.
razor_html_raw.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

service_worker_hijack.name: Service Worker Hijack
service_worker_hijack.risk: A Service Worker at root scope (/) intercepts ALL requests. If XSS is possible, the attacker controls all network traffic permanently (CWE-349).
service_worker_hijack.solution: Register Service Workers with the narrowest possible scope. Use Content-Security-Policy to restrict service worker sources.
service_worker_hijack.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

spring_actuator_exposed.name: Spring Actuator Exposed
spring_actuator_exposed.risk: /actuator/env exposes all configuration including secrets. /actuator/heapdump can leak credentials from memory (CWE-215).
spring_actuator_exposed.solution: Restrict to health and info only. Require authentication for all actuator endpoints.
spring_actuator_exposed.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

sql_injection_java_broad.name: SQL Injection (Java)
sql_injection_java_broad.risk: SQL query executed in a file containing HTTP request parameters — potential SQL injection (CWE-89).
sql_injection_java_broad.solution: Use parameterized queries with PreparedStatement and bound parameters.
sql_injection_java_broad.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

ssrf.name: SSRF (Generic)
ssrf.risk: An attacker can make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary URLs, including internal services.
ssrf.solution: Validate and whitelist allowed URLs/domains before making outgoing requests.
ssrf.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

ssrf_pdf_generation.name: SSRF via PDF Generation
ssrf_pdf_generation.risk: PDF generators like wkhtmltopdf, WeasyPrint, and Puppeteer make HTTP requests to the provided URL. An attacker can target internal services (CWE-918).
ssrf_pdf_generation.solution: Validate URLs against an allowlist. Block private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x).
ssrf_pdf_generation.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_codeinj.name: Taint Code Injection
taint_codeinj.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server.
taint_codeinj.solution: Replace dynamic execution with ast.literal_eval() for data parsing, or use a whitelist of allowed operations.
taint_codeinj.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_deserialization.name: Taint Deserialization
taint_deserialization.risk: An attacker can achieve remote code execution by sending crafted serialized Java objects.
taint_deserialization.solution: Use ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+) or ValidatingObjectInputStream from Apache Commons.
taint_deserialization.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_ldap.name: Taint LDAP Injection
taint_ldap.risk: An attacker can modify LDAP queries to bypass authentication or extract data.
taint_ldap.solution: Use LdapEncoder.filterEncode() to sanitize input before LDAP queries.
taint_ldap.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_log_injection.name: Taint Log Injection
taint_log_injection.risk: An attacker can forge log entries, hide traces, or exploit log processing tools.
taint_log_injection.solution: Sanitize user input before logging by removing newlines and control characters.
taint_log_injection.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_open_redirect.name: Taint Open Redirect
taint_open_redirect.risk: An attacker can redirect users to a malicious site via a crafted URL.
taint_open_redirect.solution: Validate redirect targets against an allowlist. Use url_for() for internal redirects.
taint_open_redirect.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_path_traversal.name: Taint Path Traversal
taint_path_traversal.risk: An attacker can read or write arbitrary files on the server.
taint_path_traversal.solution: Use path.basename() and validate the resolved path stays within the allowed directory.
taint_path_traversal.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_rce.name: Taint RCE
taint_rce.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary commands.
taint_rce.solution: Avoid Runtime.exec with user input; use ProcessBuilder with argument lists.
taint_rce.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_sqli.name: Taint SQL Injection
taint_sqli.risk: An attacker can read, modify, or delete database records.
taint_sqli.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_ssrf.name: Taint SSRF
taint_ssrf.risk: An attacker can make the server send requests to internal services.
taint_ssrf.solution: Validate URLs with Uri.TryCreate and check against an allowlist.
taint_ssrf.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_ssti.name: Taint SSTI
taint_ssti.risk: An attacker can execute arbitrary code via template injection, often leading to full RCE.
taint_ssti.solution: Never pass user input directly to template engines. Use sandboxed environments or pre-compiled templates.
taint_ssti.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xpathi.name: Taint XPath Injection
taint_xpathi.risk: An attacker can manipulate XPath queries to bypass authentication or extract XML data.
taint_xpathi.solution: Use parameterized XPath queries with variables parameter, or validate/escape user input.
taint_xpathi.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xss.name: Taint XSS
taint_xss.risk: An attacker can inject malicious scripts that execute in other users' browsers.
taint_xss.solution: Escape all user input before rendering in HTML. Use framework auto-escaping or html.escape().
taint_xss.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

taint_xxe.name: Taint XXE
taint_xxe.risk: An attacker can read local files, perform SSRF, or cause DoS via malicious XML.
taint_xxe.solution: Disable external entity processing: setFeature(DISALLOW_DOCTYPE, true).
taint_xxe.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

trust_boundary_java.name: Trust Boundary Violation
trust_boundary_java.risk: User input stored in HTTP session without validation crosses trust boundary (CWE-501).
trust_boundary_java.solution: Validate and sanitize all user input before storing in session.
trust_boundary_java.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

weak_cipher_java.name: Weak Cipher (Java)
weak_cipher_java.risk: Weak cipher algorithm (DES, RC2, RC4) provides insufficient encryption strength (CWE-327).
weak_cipher_java.solution: Use AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 for encryption.
weak_cipher_java.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

weak_password_hash.name: Weak Password Hash
weak_password_hash.risk: SHA-256/SHA-512 are fast hashes, not key derivation functions. Passwords hashed with SHA can be cracked in seconds with GPU (CWE-916).
weak_password_hash.solution: Use bcrypt.hashpw(), argon2.hash(), or passlib.hash.pbkdf2_sha256. Never use hashlib for passwords.
weak_password_hash.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

weak_random_java_util.name: Weak Random (Java)
weak_random_java_util.risk: java.util.Random is not cryptographically secure. Predictable values enable session hijacking or token forgery (CWE-330).
weak_random_java_util.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

websocket_no_validation.name: WebSocket No Validation
websocket_no_validation.risk: Unvalidated WebSocket messages can contain injection payloads, oversized data, or malformed structures (CWE-20).
websocket_no_validation.solution: Validate all incoming WebSocket messages against a schema (Zod, Joi, Ajv). Limit message size.
websocket_no_validation.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

xpath_injection_java_eval.name: XPath Injection (Java)
xpath_injection_java_eval.risk: XPath expression built with user input via string concatenation enables data extraction (CWE-643).
xpath_injection_java_eval.solution: Use parameterized XPath queries with XPathVariableResolver instead of string concatenation.
xpath_injection_java_eval.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

xss_servlet_response.name: XSS Servlet Response
xss_servlet_response.risk: User input written directly to HTTP response without encoding enables reflected XSS (CWE-79).
xss_servlet_response.solution: Use OWASP ESAPI encoder or HTML-escape all user input before writing to response.
xss_servlet_response.benefit: Reduces attack surface and strengthens application security.

db_tls_disabled_java.name: DB connection without TLS (Java)
db_tls_disabled_java.risk: The JDBC connection has SSL/TLS disabled or certificate verification turned off. All database traffic is transmitted in cleartext and can be intercepted (CWE-327).
db_tls_disabled_java.solution: Enable SSL/TLS: append ?useSSL=true&verifyServerCertificate=true to MySQL JDBC URL, or ?ssl=true&sslmode=verify-full for PostgreSQL JDBC.
db_tls_disabled_java.benefit: Encrypts all data in transit between the Java application and the database (OWASP A02, CWE-327).

db_superuser_connection_python.name: DB connection as superuser (Python)
db_superuser_connection_python.risk: A database connection uses a privileged account (root, sa, admin, postgres). A compromised application can read, modify, or delete any data (CWE-250).
db_superuser_connection_python.solution: Create a dedicated database user with only the permissions required. Never use root, sa, postgres, or admin accounts in production code.
