db_superuser_connection_python.benefit: Limits blast radius of a compromised application to only the tables the service needs (OWASP A01, CWE-250).

redis_eval_injection_python.name: Redis EVAL injection (Python)
redis_eval_injection_python.risk: A Redis EVAL command executes a Lua script built from user-controlled input. An attacker can inject arbitrary Lua code to read/modify any Redis key (CWE-943).
redis_eval_injection_python.solution: Pass user data as KEYS or ARGV arguments to EVAL, never interpolate them into the Lua script. Keep the Lua script as a static string literal.
redis_eval_injection_python.benefit: Prevents arbitrary Lua code execution and unauthorized Redis data access (OWASP A03, CWE-943).

redis_eval_injection_js.name: Redis EVAL injection (JavaScript)
redis_eval_injection_js.risk: A Redis EVAL command executes a Lua script that includes user-controlled data. An attacker can inject Lua code to bypass rate limits or escalate privileges (CWE-943).
redis_eval_injection_js.solution: Keep the Lua script as a static string. Pass user data as KEYS or ARGV arguments.
redis_eval_injection_js.benefit: Prevents Lua code injection into Redis, protecting data integrity and access controls (OWASP A03, CWE-943).

stored_procedure_dynamic_csharp.name: Dynamic stored procedure (C#)
stored_procedure_dynamic_csharp.risk: A stored procedure call is built by concatenating user input into an EXEC statement. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL commands (CWE-89).
stored_procedure_dynamic_csharp.solution: Use SqlParameter for all user-supplied values. Never concatenate user input into EXEC or sp_executesql strings.
stored_procedure_dynamic_csharp.benefit: Eliminates dynamic SQL injection via stored procedure calls (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

stored_procedure_dynamic_java.name: Dynamic stored procedure (Java)
stored_procedure_dynamic_java.risk: A stored procedure call is built by concatenating user input into an EXEC or CALL statement. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL commands (CWE-89).
stored_procedure_dynamic_java.solution: Use CallableStatement with parameterized placeholders. Never concatenate user input into stored procedure calls.
stored_procedure_dynamic_java.benefit: Eliminates stored procedure injection by enforcing parameterized calls (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

unbounded_query_js.name: Unbounded query (JavaScript)
unbounded_query_js.risk: A query without LIMIT or pagination (find({}), findAll()) can return all documents, causing memory exhaustion and request timeouts (CWE-770).
unbounded_query_js.solution: Add a limit: Model.find({}).limit(100). Use pagination: accept page/limit from validated params and enforce a maximum page size.
unbounded_query_js.benefit: Prevents denial of service through unbounded result sets (OWASP A04, CWE-770).

unbounded_query_java.name: Unbounded query (Java)
unbounded_query_java.risk: repository.findAll() or getResultList() without pagination can return every row in the table, causing OOM errors and request timeouts (CWE-770).
unbounded_query_java.solution: Use Spring Data Pageable: repository.findAll(PageRequest.of(page, size)). For JPA: query.setMaxResults(100).setFirstResult(offset).
unbounded_query_java.benefit: Prevents memory exhaustion and timeouts on large datasets (OWASP A04, CWE-770).

unbounded_query_php.name: Unbounded query (PHP)
unbounded_query_php.risk: Queries without LIMIT (::all(), fetchAll()) can return every row in the table, causing memory exhaustion and PHP max_memory errors (CWE-770).
unbounded_query_php.solution: For Laravel: use paginate() instead of all(). For PDO: add LIMIT ? OFFSET ? to the SQL query.
unbounded_query_php.benefit: Prevents memory exhaustion and denial of service on large tables (OWASP A04, CWE-770).

stored_procedure_dynamic_php.name: Dynamic stored procedure (PHP)
stored_procedure_dynamic_php.risk: A stored procedure call built by concatenating a PHP variable into EXEC or CALL allows SQL injection through the concatenated value (CWE-89).
stored_procedure_dynamic_php.solution: Use PDO prepared statements: $stmt = $pdo->prepare('CALL GetUser(:id)'); $stmt->bindParam(':id', $userId, PDO::PARAM_INT).
stored_procedure_dynamic_php.benefit: Eliminates stored procedure injection by enforcing parameterized calls (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

db_superuser_connection_java.name: DB connection as superuser (Java)
db_superuser_connection_java.risk: A JDBC connection uses a privileged account (root, sa, admin, postgres). A compromised application can read, modify, or delete any data (CWE-250).
db_superuser_connection_java.solution: Create a dedicated database user with minimum permissions. Store credentials in environment variables or a secrets manager.
db_superuser_connection_java.benefit: Limits blast radius of a compromised application (OWASP A01, CWE-250).

elasticsearch_query_injection.name: Elasticsearch query injection (Python)
elasticsearch_query_injection.risk: An Elasticsearch query body constructed from user input allows DSL injection: script execution, filter bypass, or DoS via expensive aggregations (CWE-943).
elasticsearch_query_injection.solution: Never pass user input directly as query body. Build a fixed query structure and inject only validated scalar values into specific fields.
elasticsearch_query_injection.benefit: Prevents unauthorized data extraction and DoS via crafted Elasticsearch DSL injections (OWASP A03, CWE-943).

n_plus_1_query_js.name: N+1 query (JavaScript)
n_plus_1_query_js.risk: An async database query inside a loop triggers one query per iteration, causing exponential database load and response time degradation (CWE-770).
n_plus_1_query_js.solution: Use bulk fetching: collect all IDs then fetch with findAll({ where: { id: ids } }). Use ORM eager loading (include) to fetch related data in a single query.
n_plus_1_query_js.benefit: Reduces database load from O(N) queries to O(1), improving response time and scalability (OWASP A04, CWE-770).

n_plus_1_query_php.name: N+1 query (PHP)
n_plus_1_query_php.risk: A database query inside a foreach loop triggers one query per iteration — N+1 queries for N records — causing exponential load and high memory usage (CWE-770).
n_plus_1_query_php.solution: For Laravel Eloquent: use with() eager loading. For raw queries: collect IDs and use a single WHERE IN query. Use chunk() for large datasets.
n_plus_1_query_php.benefit: Reduces database queries from N+1 to 1-2, eliminating the most common PHP performance bottleneck (OWASP A04, CWE-770).

mass_assignment_java.name: Mass assignment (Java)
mass_assignment_java.risk: BeanUtils.copyProperties() or populate() with an HTTP request copies all request parameters onto the model, including sensitive fields like role or isAdmin (CWE-915).
mass_assignment_java.solution: Use a DTO with only the fields the user should set. Validate with @Valid. Use @JsonIgnore to exclude sensitive fields.
mass_assignment_java.benefit: Prevents privilege escalation by ensuring only declared fields can be bound from HTTP requests (OWASP A01, CWE-915).

mass_assignment_csharp.name: Mass assignment (C#)
mass_assignment_csharp.risk: TryUpdateModelAsync() or UpdateModel() without an explicit field whitelist binds all request parameters to the model, including sensitive fields (CWE-915).
mass_assignment_csharp.solution: Pass an explicit field whitelist: TryUpdateModelAsync(model, "", m => m.Name, m => m.Email). Use view models (DTOs). Apply [Bind(Include="...")] attribute.
mass_assignment_csharp.benefit: Prevents mass assignment attacks that escalate privileges or corrupt business-critical fields (OWASP A01, CWE-915).

db_error_exposed_java.name: DB error exposed in response (Java)
db_error_exposed_java.risk: A database exception message returned in the HTTP response reveals table names, column names, SQL structure, or library versions that help attackers craft exploits (CWE-209).
db_error_exposed_java.solution: Return a generic HTTP 500 message. Log the full exception server-side with SLF4J/Logback. Use @ControllerAdvice with @ExceptionHandler to centralize error handling.
db_error_exposed_java.benefit: Prevents database reconnaissance enabling targeted SQL injection and data extraction attacks (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

db_connection_string_credentials.name: DB connection string with credentials (Python)
db_connection_string_credentials.risk: A database connection URL with embedded credentials (user:password@host) stores plaintext secrets in source code, visible in version control history (CWE-522, CWE-798).
db_connection_string_credentials.solution: Store the URL in an environment variable: DATABASE_URL = os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]. Use a secrets manager in production. Add .env files to .gitignore.
db_connection_string_credentials.benefit: Prevents credential exposure via source code and version control history (OWASP A02, CWE-798).

sql_injection_format_string_python.name: SQL injection via % format string (Python)
sql_injection_format_string_python.risk: A SQL query built with Python's % string operator instead of parameterized queries allows an attacker to inject SQL by controlling the formatted values (CWE-89).
sql_injection_format_string_python.solution: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("SELECT ... WHERE name = %s", (name,)). The DB driver handles escaping safely.
sql_injection_format_string_python.benefit: Eliminates SQL injection via Python string formatting (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

hardcoded_connection_string_java.name: Hardcoded DB credentials (Java)
hardcoded_connection_string_java.risk: A JDBC connection uses a hardcoded password literal or embedded credentials in the URL. Credentials in source code appear in version control history (CWE-798).
hardcoded_connection_string_java.solution: Read credentials from environment variables: System.getenv("DB_PASSWORD"). In Spring Boot, use ${DB_PASSWORD} in application.properties backed by environment variables.
hardcoded_connection_string_java.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history (OWASP A02, CWE-798).

hardcoded_connection_string_php.name: Hardcoded DB credentials (PHP)
hardcoded_connection_string_php.risk: A database connection uses a hardcoded password literal as a direct argument to PDO, mysqli, or mysql_connect. Credentials in source code appear in version control history (CWE-798).
hardcoded_connection_string_php.solution: Read the password from environment variables: getenv('DB_PASSWORD'). Use vlucas/phpdotenv for .env files. Never commit .env files to version control.
hardcoded_connection_string_php.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history (OWASP A02, CWE-798).

db_superuser_connection_csharp.name: DB connection as superuser (C#)
db_superuser_connection_csharp.risk: A SQL Server connection string uses a privileged account (sa, root, admin). A compromised application can read, modify, or delete any data, and execute OS commands via xp_cmdshell (CWE-250).
db_superuser_connection_csharp.solution: Create a dedicated SQL login with minimum permissions. Never use sa, root, or accounts with sysadmin/db_owner role in production. Store credentials in Azure Key Vault or environment variables.
db_superuser_connection_csharp.benefit: Limits blast radius of a compromised application (OWASP A01, CWE-250).

db_error_exposed_csharp.name: DB error exposed in response (C#)
db_error_exposed_csharp.risk: A database exception message returned in the HTTP response reveals table names, column names, SQL structure, or stack traces that help attackers craft exploits (CWE-209).
db_error_exposed_csharp.solution: Return a generic HTTP 500 message. Log exceptions with ILogger. Use UseExceptionHandler() with ProblemDetails in the global pipeline.
db_error_exposed_csharp.benefit: Prevents database reconnaissance enabling targeted SQL injection attacks (OWASP A09, CWE-209).

nosql_document_parse_java.name: MongoDB Document.parse injection (Java)
nosql_document_parse_java.risk: Document.parse() called with a variable can execute arbitrary MongoDB operators ($where, $regex, $gt) if the variable contains user-controlled JSON, bypassing access filters (CWE-943).
nosql_document_parse_java.solution: Use the Filters builder API: Filters.eq("field", value). Never pass user input directly to Document.parse(). Validate and whitelist allowed filter fields.
nosql_document_parse_java.benefit: Prevents NoSQL injection that bypasses authentication and authorization filters (OWASP A03, CWE-943).

sql_injection_raw_js.name: SQL injection in raw query (JavaScript)
sql_injection_raw_js.risk: A raw database query (mysql2, pg) built by string concatenation or template literal allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL (CWE-89).
sql_injection_raw_js.solution: Use parameterized queries: pool.query("SELECT ... WHERE id = $1", [id]) for pg, pool.query("... WHERE id = ?", [id]) for mysql2.
sql_injection_raw_js.benefit: Eliminates SQL injection in raw database calls (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

sql_order_by_injection_python.name: ORDER BY injection (Python)
sql_order_by_injection_python.risk: The ORDER BY clause is constructed from user-controlled input without validation, allowing injection of additional SQL or boolean-based blind injection (CWE-89).
sql_order_by_injection_python.solution: Validate the sort column against an explicit whitelist: ALLOWED_SORT = {'name', 'price'}; if sort_col not in ALLOWED_SORT: sort_col = 'name'.
sql_order_by_injection_python.benefit: Prevents ORDER BY injection enabling blind SQL injection and data extraction (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

nosql_operator_injection_python.name: MongoDB operator injection (Python)
nosql_operator_injection_python.risk: A MongoDB query uses $where or constructs operators ($regex, $gt) with user-controlled input. $where executes JavaScript server-side, enabling data exfiltration or authentication bypass (CWE-943).
nosql_operator_injection_python.solution: Never use $where with user input. Use standard equality operators: {"username": username_string}. For text search, use $text with indexed fields.
nosql_operator_injection_python.benefit: Prevents server-side JavaScript execution and operator injection that bypass MongoDB access controls (OWASP A03, CWE-943).

insecure_db_deserialization_python.name: Insecure DB deserialization (Python)
insecure_db_deserialization_python.risk: Data from a database is deserialized with pickle.loads(). An attacker who can modify stored data can achieve remote code execution via a malicious pickle payload (CWE-502).
insecure_db_deserialization_python.solution: Use JSON or MessagePack for structured data. If binary blobs are required, verify integrity with cryptographic signing before deserialization.
insecure_db_deserialization_python.benefit: Prevents remote code execution via malicious payloads injected into database storage (OWASP A08, CWE-502).

db_connection_string_credentials_js.name: DB connection string with credentials (JavaScript)
db_connection_string_credentials_js.risk: A database URL with embedded credentials (protocol://user:password@host) stores plaintext secrets in source code, visible in version control history (CWE-798).
db_connection_string_credentials_js.solution: Store the URL in an environment variable: const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL. Use a secrets manager in production. Add .env files to .gitignore.
db_connection_string_credentials_js.benefit: Prevents database credential exposure via source code and version control history (OWASP A02, CWE-798).

sql_injection_string_format_csharp.name: SQL injection via string.Format (C#)
sql_injection_string_format_csharp.risk: A SQL query built with string.Format() embeds user-controlled values directly in the query string, allowing SQL injection via malicious format arguments (CWE-89).
sql_injection_string_format_csharp.solution: Use SqlParameter: cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", name). For EF Core, use ExecuteSqlInterpolated() instead of ExecuteSqlRaw() with string.Format.
sql_injection_string_format_csharp.benefit: Eliminates SQL injection via string.Format() by enforcing parameterized query usage (OWASP A03, CWE-89).

SECURITY.title: Security & OWASP
SECURITY.risk: Security vulnerabilities allow attackers to steal data, execute malicious code, or compromise the system.
SECURITY.solution: Use parameterized queries for SQL, textContent or a secure template system for DOM, and never hardcode secrets.
SECURITY.benefit: Immunity against SQL injections, XSS, and OWASP Top 10 compliance.

ARCH.title: Architecture & Patterns
ARCH.risk: Scattered business logic makes code difficult to test and causes duplication.
ARCH.solution: Centralize logic in Services, keep Routers minimal.
ARCH.benefit: Modular, testable code compliant with best practices.

UI.title: Interface & Rendering
UI.risk: Direct DOM manipulation is slow, insecure and makes debugging difficult.
UI.solution: Use a secure template system for all HTML rendering.
UI.benefit: Improved performance, XSS security, visual consistency.

UX.title: User Experience
UX.risk: Transient and untranslated notifications frustrate users and reduce accessibility.
UX.solution: Translate all user-facing text, make error messages persistent.
UX.benefit: Better accessibility, multi-language support, professional UX.

MAINTENANCE.title: Maintenance & DRY
MAINTENANCE.risk: Dead and duplicated code increases cognitive load and the risk of bugs.
MAINTENANCE.solution: Remove unused code, share common logic in modules.

DEPENDENCIES.title: Dependencies
DEPENDENCIES.risk: Vulnerable or unpinned dependencies expose the project to known attacks.
DEPENDENCIES.solution: Update vulnerable dependencies and pin exact versions.
DEPENDENCIES.benefit: Elimination of known CVEs, reproducible builds (OWASP A06).

DATABASE.title: PostgreSQL Schema
DATABASE.risk: Undetected schema changes can cause runtime errors.
DATABASE.solution: Check migrations, update code referencing modified elements.
DATABASE.benefit: Schema stability, early detection of breaking changes.

CICD.title: CI/CD Pipelines
CICD.risk: Misconfigured CI/CD pipelines expose the project to supply chain attacks.
CICD.solution: Pin actions by SHA, restrict permissions, validate triggers.
CICD.benefit: Protection against supply chain attacks (OWASP CI-CD Top 10).
